Title: Kepong MP wants IGP to explain double standards over Jalur Gemilang display errors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A government backbencher today called on Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail to explain allegations of double standards in investigations into cases involving the incorrect display of the Jalur Gemilang.
Kepong member of Parliament Lim Lip Eng said if the mistake in displaying the Jalur Gemilang was genuinely unintentional, promptly corrected and followed by an apology, no one should be arrested.
"My position is clear. However, in the Kulai case, two people were detained and remanded for four days, and even underwent urine tests.
"In the Perak MCA case, those involved were only called in to have their statements recorded without being detained.
"When Kuala Terengganu City Council displayed the Jalur Gemilang without the crescent and star, the explanation of a 'technical error' was accepted and no arrests were reported," he said in a statement.
He claimed that in the cases, the authorities had treated those responsible differently.
"The mistakes were almost identical, but the police treatment was vastly different. Does police action depend on who is involved?
"The Inspector-General of Police must immediately explain this double standard," he said.
Lim said that if Khalid failed to provide a reasonable explanation or continued to remain silent as in the Kulai case, he should resign immediately.
"The police cannot act harshly against ordinary citizens but be lenient when it involves 'VIPs' and government agencies.
"That is not justice. That is favouritism," he said.
In the latest case, Perak MCA took full responsibility for the mistake of displaying the Jalur Gemilang and Perak state flag upside down, which went viral yesterday. The staff member involved has since resigned.
Perak MCA State Liaison Committee chairman Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon said the party took the incident seriously and apologised to the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, as well as all Malaysians over the mistake.

Title: Ahmad Zahid congratulates Wakaf Tapai IKBN student on international championship win
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has congratulated Wakaf Tapai National Youth Skills Institute (IKBN) student Muhammad Ammar Azli on winning the welding category at the Finals of the Professional Skills Championship (Professionals 2026) in Kaluga, Russia.
The Rural and Regional Development Minister said the achievement once again demonstrated that the country's technical and vocational education and training (TVET) students have the talent and skills to compete with the world's best on the international stage.
"Congratulations, Muhammad Ammar! Seeing the Jalur Gemilang flying on the international stage, thanks to the skills of a young TVET student, is certainly a source of pride for all of us.
"I would also like to congratulate the instructors and the entire Wakaf Tapai IKBN and Youth and Sports Skills Training Institute (ILKBS) community who guided and prepared him for this achievement," he said in a Facebook post today.
Ahmad Zahid said that after his success in Russia, Muhammad Ammar would next take on the challenge of representing the country at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 this September, expressing hope that he would continue to excel and give his best for Malaysia.
"May this achievement inspire more young people to see TVET as a pathway to acquiring skills, building careers and securing their future. Insya-Allah," he said. — BERNAMA

Title: Retired soldiers turn homes into 'Galeri Merdeka' with 300 Jalur Gemilang flags
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Their days in military service may be over, but Yusof Abu Talib and Abd Razak Mohd Jai continue to show their patriotism and love for the country by turning their homes into what they describe as "Galeri Merdeka".
In conjunction with this year's 69th National Day celebrations, the two in-laws, who live in neighbouring houses, have adorned their homes in Kampung Lendu, here, with more than 300 Jalur Gemilang flags and various Independence-themed decorations.
Their efforts have turned their homes into a colourful attraction for villagers, offering them a place to experience the spirit of patriotism in a relaxed and community-oriented setting.
[[nid:1521154]]
Yusof, 54, said the idea stemmed from their desire to continue fostering love for the country even though they were no longer serving in the military.
"We have served the country and that spirit has never faded. After retiring, we thought about what we could do to continue contributing to the community.
"To us, the Jalur Gemilang is not just a flag.
"It symbolises the struggle, sacrifice and independence that every citizen should appreciate," he said.
He said the initiative also features various collections and materials related to independence as part of efforts to introduce the country's history and foster love for the country, particularly among the younger generation.
[[nid:1521153]]
The gallery also documents the incident involving their father-in-law, the late Zakaria Ibrahim, who was ambushed by communist insurgents and died in Gerik, Perak, around 1979.
Both men put up the Jalur Gemilang flags around their homes with the help of their respective families.
Razak, 65, said seeing the flags flying around their homes evoked a strong sense of pride in being Malaysians who were free from colonial rule.
[[nid:1521152]]
He said the initiative was also part of their efforts to enliven the country's National Day celebrations, alongside a Jalur Gemilang decoration competition held in the village.
For him, the competition was not merely aimed at beautifying the residential area, but also served as a platform to strengthen community ties and foster patriotism.

Title: Merdeka Day parade to proceed if clear skies remain
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Merdeka Day parade on Monday will proceed as scheduled if clear skies remain, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said a meeting was held yesterday afternoon involving the Meteorological Department, Environment Department, Health Ministry and Education Ministry.
"We have decided that if conditions remain as they are this morning (clear skies) and yesterday, we will proceed with the event on Monday," he said after the National Day 2026 parade rehearsal in Putrajaya today.

Title: CIMB doubles down on dividend payout of above 55pct despite Indonesia headwinds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd is doubling down on its dividend payout ratio of above 55 per cent despite challenges in Indonesia, group chief executive officer Novan Amirudin said.
He said CIMB, Malaysia's second-largest bank by assets, has multiple "levers" it can pull across its diversified regional operations to support earnings and keep its dividend policy intact.
"Our payout ratio has consistently been above 55 per cent over the last few years. There will be no change to that," he said at the group's second-quarter results briefing yesterday.
"Yes, there are challenges in Indonesia, but that is the strength of the CIMB franchise. We are a diversified business," he said.
Novan said Malaysia and Singapore continued to perform strongly, while Thailand was undergoing a transformation into a wealth and wholesale-focused business.
This follows the group's move to dispose of its loss-making automotive financing portfolio in Thailand, which is expected to be completed this year.
"We have many levers for our business," Novan said.
Group chief financial officer Khairul Rifaie said the bank's net interest income (NII) growth was underpinned by strong total asset growth, supported by a healthy pipeline that would continue to drive NII growth.
"However, partially offsetting that, we are facing some net interest margin (NIM) pressure. We expect group NIM to be between stable and down by 10 basis points year-on-year.
"Margins contracted in the first half and we expect that headwind to continue. But with a strong pipeline of asset growth, we should still record moderate to good NII growth, which will translate to profit before tax," he said.
Meanwhile, Khairul said CIMB Group was targeting loan growth of around five to six per cent this year, while its gross impaired loan ratio was expected to remain relatively stable, although some pockets of deterioration could emerge.
"We do see other pockets of improvement because of the underlying trend, but there could be some areas where it is more exposed indirectly to the Middle East pressure or inflationary cost pressure, where you might see some small pickup in terms of impaired loans. But the overall group number should be relatively stable," he said.
The bank maintained its financial year 2026 guidance, including a return on equity of 11 to 11.5 per cent, asset growth of five to seven per cent on a constant-currency basis and a cost-to-income ratio below 47 per cent.
It also retained its guidance for loan loss charges of 25 to 35 basis points and a common equity tier-one ratio of 14 per cent.

Title: Trump announces new US 'Space Academy'
Article:
Trump announces new US 'Space Academy'
AFP
JOHNSON SPACE CENTRE: President Donald Trump on Friday announced the creation of a "Space Academy" to train future civilian and military recruits for an arena where the United States faces rivalry with China.
Speaking at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, Trump said the institution would be modeled on the famed US military academy at West Point.
"It's called the U.S. Space Academy. That's a big deal," Trump said as he signed an executive order creating the new school.
"It'll serve both the United States Space Force as well as NASA and the civilian spaceflight industry, and it'll attract, train, and graduate the very best of our nation."
Trump has credited the US Space Force, the sixth branch of the US armed forces, with an important role in the recent American military operations in Venezuela and Iran.
He did not say where the new academy would be built.
The US president also presented the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the crew of NASA's Artemis 2 mission, which flew past the moon in April.
Outer space has become an increasingly strategic domain for global powers in the military and technology fields.
The United States is competing with China in the race to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, more than 50 years after humans first walked the lunar surface.
Trump last week pledged a "golden age" of space in a push to launch more rockets, including to Mars and the Moon.

Title: Perak to consider RM500 first-marriage incentive under 2027 state budget
Article:
IPOH: A proposal to introduce a RM500 First-Time Marriage Incentive for youths in Perak will be submitted to the relevant State Executive Council (Exco) member for further discussion and refinement before being considered under the 2027 state budget.
Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said the motion proposing the special incentive was unanimously approved during the recent fifth sitting of the Perak Youth Assembly.
He said the proposal reflected the state government's concern and commitment to helping ease the financial burden faced by young people entering marriage.
"We view this as a positive initiative that demonstrates the state government's care and concern by providing some assistance to newly married couples," he told reporters after representing Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad at the presentation of the state-level National Youth Premier Award and State Youth Special Award 2026 here last night.
Khairudin said the proposed assistance would target youths aged between 15 and 35, in line with the definition of youth under the Youth Development and Sports Act 2007.
He added that specific eligibility criteria would also be established, including requiring applicants to be Perak natives or to have resided in the state for at least 10 years.
However, he said the final details and implementation of the proposed incentive would be subject to deliberation and approval by the State Executive Council before any official announcement was made.
"The proposal is expected to be finalised ahead of the presentation of the state budget in November," he said.
Meanwhile, Khairudin said the National Youth Premier Award featured three categories, namely male individual, female individual and youth organisation, while the State Youth Special Award comprised seven categories, all fully funded by the state government.
"I hope the winners tonight will serve as a source of inspiration and motivation for young people, particularly youths in Perak, to become actively involved in youth organisations and, in the process, develop leadership qualities, skills, a spirit of volunteerism and integrity," he said.
Khairudin said all recipients underwent a comprehensive assessment by an independent panel comprising youth development experts and former state youth leaders.
Winners of both the National Youth Premier Award and State Youth Special Award received trophies and certificates, along with cash prizes ranging from RM1,000 to RM10,000, depending on their placing in their respective categories.
In the male individual category of the state-level National Youth Premier Award, Muhammad Amizan Lokman, 28, representing Hulu Perak, emerged as the winner, followed by Muhammad Saiful Hanif Khairi, 29, representing Muallim, as runner-up, and Muhammad Awliya Mohd Fauzi, 25, representing Kerian, in third place.
In the female individual category, M. Ashhwina, 20, representing Larut Matang, took first place, followed by C. Vhainmathy, 21, representing Kerian, as runner-up, and Nicole Tiuk Yu Xuan, 20, representing Hilir Perak, in third place.
Meanwhile, the Larut Matang District Youth Council emerged as the winner in the youth organisation category, followed by the Federation of Malay Students of the Peninsula (Ipoh Branch) and the Malaysian Youth Clubs Association (Teluk Intan Area).
Winners of the 2026 Perak State Youth Special Award received RM2,000 in cash, along with a trophy and certificate, in each of the seven contested categories: charisma, entrepreneurship, resilience, young volunteerism, sports, persons with disabilities and uniformed associations.

Title: Penang factory fire leaves owner with first-degree burns
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: The owner of a fabric-processing factory suffered first-degree burns to his hands and neck while trying to put out a fire that destroyed about 80 per cent of his premises in Jalan Bagan Ajam here yesterday afternoon.
The 58-year-old man was taken to a nearby hospital for medical treatment.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 6.09pm.
"The fire involved a factory that processed fabric for use in sofas.
The fire also damaged two motorcycles by 50 per cent each, a four-tonne lorry by 90 per cent and a forklift by 90 per cent.
"The fire was brought under control at 6.28pm, with firefighting efforts also assisted by the nearby Volunteer Fire Brigade and an excavator belonging to a private company," he said in a statement.
He said firefighters took almost 10 hours to completely extinguish the fire.
"The fire was completely extinguished at 4.35am today," he said.
The operation ended at 6.59am, after which the case was handed over to the Fire Investigation Team.
A total of 26 personnel, including station chiefs, from the Butterworth, Penanti, Kepala Batas, Jalan Perak, Bandar Perda, Bertam and Perai Fire and Rescue Stations took part in the operation.

Title: Fire destroys 80 per cent of food stall, storage facility in Ampang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A food stall and a storage facility were almost destroyed in a fire in front of a school near Pekan Ampang, Ampang, here, early this morning.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said a team from the Ampang Fire and Rescue Station was deployed to the scene after the department received an emergency call at 3.46am.
He said the fire involved two premises owned by different people, namely a food stall and a general storage facility.
"About 80 per cent of both premises were destroyed in the fire, but no casualties were reported," he said.
He said the operation ended at 8.30am.

Title: Patriotism flies high all year at Nor Ashikin's Jalur Gemilang-adorned home
Article:
JERTIH: Upon stepping into the compound of her home, one's attention is immediately drawn to the fluttering Jalur Gemilang and colourful patriotic decorations adorning almost every corner, creating the impression that National Month is celebrated there all year round.
For local food vendor Nor Ashikin Shafiee, 42, decorating her home in Kampung Baru Tok Dor with patriotic-themed ornaments has become a way of life.
Since getting married and moving into her own home more than two decades ago, she has made the Jalur Gemilang and colourful decorations a permanent feature of her residence.
She said her passion for decorating went beyond simply beautifying her home, describing it as her personal way of nurturing patriotism in her daily life.
"Most of these decorations remain up throughout the year and are only replaced when they become worn out.
"However, when National Month approaches, I replace them with new ones to further enliven the spirit of independence.
"For this year's National Month, I spent more than RM1,000, including on replacing over 80 metres of fabric and curtains, as well as dozens of umbrellas, flags and various other accessories to spruce up the house," she said when met at her home recently.
Nor Ashikin said her passion for decorating and maintaining a clean and cheerful home was inherited from her father, who instilled in her and her sister from a young age the importance of keeping their surroundings tidy and pleasant.
[[nid:1521163]]
The mother of two also personally sews some of the decorations, including curtains, to complement the colour theme chosen each year.
She said preparations for this year's National Month decorations began gradually early this month, with red, white, blue and yellow selected as the dominant colours to create a patriotic atmosphere.
Nor Ashikin added that although her income from her food business fluctuated, she continued to set aside part of her earnings to purchase new decorations or replace those that had become worn out.
She said her husband and children understood and supported her passion and did not consider the money spent on decorating the home a waste.
"Every day, I spend about an hour tidying the house and making sure the decorations inside and outside are neat before heading out to run my business.
"I am delighted that my home often attracts people who want to take photographs, especially during festive seasons and now, in conjunction with National Month," she said.
For Nor Ashikin, the patriotic decorations adorning her home do more than simply beautify the surroundings.
They serve as a daily reminder to continue nurturing her love for the country and the spirit of patriotism.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah band Tompuvan wins Asian Folk award at 2026 ICMA
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah-based Borneo ethnic fusion band Tompuvan has won The Best of Asia — Asian Folk award at the 2026 InterContinental Music Awards (ICMA) for their original song, "The Last Warrior".
"The Last Warrior" is rooted in Sabah's indigenous heritage and combines traditional Borneo sounds with contemporary music to explore survival, identity, heritage and unity.
It serves as a sonic bridge carrying the "Semengat" (Spirit) of ancestors into the modern world.
Tompuvan's Daniel Filex James said the acclaim was an achievement for the band.
"This recognition is a tremendous honour for us — not only as a music group from Sabah, but as artists committed to bringing the identity, heritage and traditional sounds of Borneo to the international stage."
Daniel co-wrote the song with Mohd Azmin Ibrahim.
Tompuvan also shared the award with Malaysian artist Elica Paujin, whose song "Oh Huminodun" was also among the five winners in the category.
The other winners were Aco Takenaka of Japan, Pooja Goswami Pavan of the United States, and Sharon Shobana Vasudevan of Singapore.
The 2026 winners were announced during the 14th Annual InterContinental Music Awards Online Awards Ceremony on Aug 23, which brought together artists and music professionals from around the world, with attendees representing 122 cities.

Title: Rantau Panjang traders optimistic school holidays will boost sales despite Narathiwat incident
Article:
PASIR MAS: Concerns among residents in the border area following a security incident in Narathiwat, Thailand, have not deterred traders in Rantau Panjang from hoping for an influx in visitors during the nine-day school holiday that began yesterday.
Last Saturday, Narathiwat province was placed under a curfew from 10.15pm to 5am following more than 50 incidents, including bombings, the burning of local government offices and tyre-burning.
The loud explosions during the incidents also shook homes and raised concerns among residents in the Malaysia-Thailand border areas, including Kampung Lubok Gong and Kampung Tersang here.
However, a Bernama survey at the Rantau Panjang Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex (ICQS) and around the town found that conditions on the second day of the school holidays remained under control, with traders expecting an increase in visitors over the weekend and ahead of National Day on Aug 31.
Food and Thai products trader Afifa Umar, 42, said although visitor numbers were currently not as high as before, the school holidays gave traders hope of increasing their income as more people visit the duty-free area.
After eight years in business, she sells various products including peanuts, cashews and sweet-and-sour fruit, and has increased her stock in preparation for higher demand.
"On normal days, sales are around RM100, but during the school holidays sthey can reach almost RM500 a day. So we have increased our stock slightly compared with normal days," she told Bernama recently.
Afifa said the increase in visitors was important not only for her business but also benefited other traders and the service sector around Rantau Panjang.
She also welcomed the development of new facilities under the Rantau Panjang Town Square and Observation Tower construction project, as well as the upgrading of the bus station, which is expected to be operational next year as they could potentially attract more visitors to the area.
She expressed hope that more visitors would return to holiday in Rantau Panjang as they did in the past, as the presence of visitors would not only enliven the area but also help boost the income of local traders.
Meanwhile, Zila Abdullah, 36, from Kampung Temangan, Machang, said she and her husband, Azhar Musa, 36, who frequently travel back and forth to Thailand, expected visitor numbers to increase ahead of National Day.
From a security perspective, Zila said the heightened presence of police, military personnel and relevant agencies gave people confidence to visit, but they should remain vigilant and comply with the authorities' instructions following the security developments in the Thai border area.
Rantau Panjang resident Azizah Mohd Tahir, 55, said visitor numbers usually increase ahead of National Day, with traffic sometimes becoming congested as far as the bridge area. — BERNAMA

Title: Trump announces deal for huge US stake in Venezuelan oil reserves
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday his administration has reached a huge oil deal with Venezuela that gives the United States majority control of 65 billion barrels of proven petroleum reserves.
The deal – which Trump proclaimed as "the biggest oil deal in world history" – will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment to Venezuela, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said.
Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves. Its government has operated under intense pressure and close scrutiny from the Trump administration since the US ousted and captured long time ruler Nicolas Maduro in January. It allowed his then vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, to stay on and serve as interim leader so long as she toes the US line.
Trump has made no secret of his desire to secure Venezuelan oil for the US, and in his post announcing the deal on his Truth Social platform, he said it will more than double US oil reserves.
There was no immediate confirmation of the arrangement from the Venezuelan government.
Trump said Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had reached the deal with Rodriguez "through a partnership with private business."
"This Transaction will greatly strengthen the already growing relationship between Venezuela and the United States!" Trump wrote.
Rubio said the deal demonstrated how "President Trump's bold foreign policy is driving America First wins: securing stable reserves and low-cost oil in our Hemisphere and lowering gas prices here at home."
"For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs, and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela's economy," the top US diplomat wrote on X, without providing further details.
The news site Axios reported Thursday the two countries were in talks on a dozen productive oil fields with 90 billion barrels of proven reserves – about a third of Venezuela's total proven reserves of 300 billion barrels. Axios quoted two US officials.
In return for a US ownership stake, private companies, including American firms, would develop the fields and return more oil revenue to Venezuela, according to Axios.
Axios also said the deal would more than double US oil reserves at a time when the US strategic petroleum reserve is at a 40-year low.
Trump also insisted the deal will lower gasoline prices for Americans – a major issue as his approval ratings fall ahead of November midterm elections after launching a war on Iran that has disrupted global oil supplies.
The Trump administration has been urging US companies to invest in Venezuela, but they remain wary due to dilapidated infrastructure and past appropriation of assets of foreign investors by the government in Caracas.
Chevron, the only US oil company that was still operating in Venezuela when Maduro was ousted, said in July that it had raised its daily crude production to 280,000 barrels and plans to increase output by 50 percent by the end of 2028.

Title: 2027 Budget will ensure country's economic sustainability and resilience, says deputy minister
Article:
KOTA BARU: The 2027 Budget, which will be tabled in October, will ensure the sustainability of the national economy so that it remains within the projected economic growth range.
Deputy Economy Minister Datuk Seri Mohd Shahar Abdullah said although economic growth forecast remained at between four and five per cent, the country's gross domestic product (GDP) growth for the second quarter stood at six per cent.
"The second quarter recorded six per cent growth, but we are not taking this as a reason to be complacent.
"We will continue to monitor the situation by holding meetings with various parties, not only industry players and associations, but also individuals.
"It is not just about one sector, but various sectors, so that we can understand what is actually happening and hear their views because we formulate policies, but they are the stakeholders.
"They understand the situation better. That is why we have increased communication through meetings of the National Economic Action Council, where we invite industry representatives to provide their views to policymakers," he said at a press conference here last night.
He added that the most important aspect was to look at the 13th Malaysia Plan, which would cover a five-year period under the budget.
"The budget is short term, but what we want to look at is the Malaysia Plan under the Economy Ministry, which covers five years.
"Whatever happens in the short term, we will manage it through the budget.
"Certainly, the budget is eagerly awaited by the people as they want to see how the government will implement various initiatives, including mitigating the impact of the global crisis," he said.
Earlier, he attended the Contractors' Fellowship Night held in conjunction with the 49th annual general meeting of the Kelantan chapter of the Malay Contractors Association of Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman prepared her brother's meals every day, until fire claimed him
Article:
KUALA NERUS: For more than a year, 62-year-old Azizah Mohd had prepared and delivered food to her younger brother every day.
Azizah never knew that yesterday would be the last time she would do so for her 60-year-old brother, Zakaria.
Azizah had been preparing ayam masak kicap (rice and soy sauce chicken) for Zakaria when a neighbour told her that her brother's house in Kampung Lingai, here, was on fire about 4pm yesterday.
She immediately rushed to the house, only to learn that Zakaria had died after he was believed to have been trapped inside the burning house.
"Every day at about 4pm, I would deliver food to my brother. Earlier, I was getting ready to send him ayam masak kicap.
"Suddenly, a neighbour told me that my brother's house was on fire. I immediately rushed there," she said when met yesterday.
In the incident about 4.50pm, Zakaria was found dead after he was believed to have been trapped inside his burning home.
Azizah said that apart from delivering food, she also bathed her brother, took care of his clothes and attended to his daily needs as he lived alone.
She said her house was about 300 metres from Zakaria's home and she would usually spend about three hours with him before returning home around 7pm.
"Whenever I went to my brother's house, we would ask each other for forgiveness before I left.
"But today, we did not have the chance to do so. I am also saddened that I did not get to bring the food to him," she said.
Azizah said their youngest brother, Harun, 54, would deliver breakfast to Zakaria at about 7.30am every day.
Meanwhile, Harun said Zakaria appeared to be his usual self when he delivered food to him yesterday morning and was waiting for him at the doorway.
"As usual, I would spend about 10 minutes with my brother before leaving for work at a shop selling hardware and carpentry equipment in Kampung Telaga Papan, here.
"At the time, I did not notice anything unusual about my brother," he said.
Harun said Zakaria lived alone, prompting the siblings to share the responsibility of delivering his meals and ensuring his daily needs were taken care of.
He said the house was not equipped with many electrical appliances or kitchen utensils and did not even have a television.
"We also do not know what caused the fire. The house's electrical wiring was replaced only about a year ago.
"This incident has affected our family because we lost a loved one in the blink of an eye.
"Nevertheless, we accept what has happened as fate," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Spain urges calm after anti-migrant protesters clash with police
Article:
MADRID: Spain's interior minister called for calm on Friday after residents of Ceuta clashed with police during protests against migrants who have remained in the North African enclave following a mass influx.
Tensions have been high in the territory of 80,000 inhabitants since tens of thousands of people crossed into Ceuta from Morocco over several days in July, triggering a Europe-wide migrant alert.
Spain's leftist government says most have since left the enclave of 18.5 square kilometres (seven square miles) but thousands remain wandering the streets and sleeping on beaches.
Demonstrations have intensified in recent days, with some protesters clashing with police on Thursday at a beach where migrants have been sleeping. Some of their belongings were burned.
A soldier was injured in a separate incident on Thursday when migrants threw stones at troops, while 12 Moroccan migrants were arrested.
Two more arrests were made after migrants attacked a police officer, sources said.
"Violence is not the answer," Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told parliament on Friday.
"I call for calm and an end to any form of violence, because... violence is not the way to resolve any problem with the complexity" of that facing Ceuta, he added.
The head of Ceuta's local government, Juan Vivas, said peaceful protests "to demand the return to normality" were justified, but warned that authorities would take action against anyone who commits acts of vandalism.
"We totally reject the use of any kind of violence," he said in an institutional address, adding: "No one can or should take the law into their own hands."
Right-wing and far-right parties have demanded that all the migrants be rounded up and sent back to their home countries.
Grande-Marlaska accused those commentators of "inciting hatred and confrontation" in Ceuta.
The government has said that each individual must be identified to determine whether they are entitled to asylum or subject to deportation, while unaccompanied migrant children require special protection.
The interior ministry said on Friday it had asked the European Commission for support from the European Union Agency for Asylum and EU border agency Frontex to help process asylum applications in Ceuta.
Ceuta and Melilla, another small Spanish territory in North Africa, have Europe's only land borders with Africa and regularly face migration pressure from people seeking to enter the EU.
Foreign Minister Jose Luis Albares described the frontier of the two territories as "the most unequal and complex border in the world to manage" and called for solidarity with Ceuta and Melilla.

Title: Haze: Sri Aman air quality worsens as API reading hits 222 this morning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality in Sri Aman, Sarawak, continued to deteriorate after the area recorded an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 222 as of 8am today.
According to the Environment Department's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 29 other areas, mostly in Sarawak, Perak and the Klang Valley, also recorded unhealthy API readings.
In Sarawak, eight air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy readings, with the Serian district police headquarters recording the highest at 193, followed by Sarikei at 188, Kuching at 169, and Samarahan and Mukah at 164 each.
Other areas in Sarawak that recorded unhealthy API readings were Sibu at 160, Kapit at 153 and Bintulu at 151.
In Perak, five air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Taiping (155), Tanjung Malim (154), Tasek Ipoh (147), Seri Manjung (119) and Pegoh Ipoh (101).
Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded unhealthy API readings of 160 and 155 respectively, while Putrajaya recorded an unhealthy API reading of 152.
In Selangor, three air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy readings, namely Shah Alam at 153, followed by Johan Setia at 151 and Petaling Jaya at 112.
Three areas in Kedah that reported unhealthy API readings were Sungai Petani (161), Langkawi (156) and Alor Setar (155).
Three areas in Penang also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Minden (160), Seberang Prai (157) and Seberang Jaya (156).
Nilai and Seremban in Negri Sembilan, Kangar in Perlis and Segamat in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings.

Title: Strengthen mental health support in schools: More than just counsellors
Article:
LETTERS:
THE mental health needs of young people are becoming increasingly complex and must be treated as a serious national priority. Schools are not only places for academic learning; they are also important environments for identifying and responding to mental health and psychosocial problems among children and adolescents.
While school counsellors play a vital role, relying solely on counsellors is no longer sufficient to meet the growing and increasingly complex needs of students.
Young people today are facing multiple pressures, including academic expectations, family problems, bullying, cyberbullying, social media pressures, online risks, relationship difficulties and uncertainty about their future. Some may also experience anxiety, depression, self-harm tendencies or other psychological difficulties requiring professional assessment and intervention.
I therefore believe that schools need a stronger multidisciplinary mental health support system, with greater access to qualified psychologists, in addition to existing school counsellors.
School counsellors should continue to provide counselling, early identification, emotional support and referrals. However, psychologists can provide more specialised assessment and intervention for students with more complex mental health needs.
There should be a clear referral pathway between schools, psychologists, government health facilities and other appropriate mental health services. Students who require specialised attention should not have to wait until their problems become severe before receiving professional help.
I would therefore suggest the following measures:
1. Increase the availability of psychologists in schools or through school-linked services, particularly in areas with large student populations.
2. Strengthen the ratio of counsellors to students, so that counsellors are not overwhelmed by excessive caseloads and administrative responsibilities.
3. Establish multidisciplinary school mental health teams, involving counsellors, psychologists, school health personnel, teachers and, where appropriate, social workers and child psychiatrists.
4. Strengthen early identification and screening, while ensuring that screening is conducted responsibly, confidentially and with appropriate professional follow-up.
5. Train teachers and school administrators to recognise early warning signs of emotional distress, behavioural changes, bullying, self-harm and other mental health concerns.
6. Improve referral and follow-up mechanisms so that students referred for professional help do not fall through the cracks between schools, families and healthcare services.
7. Engage parents more actively, because mental health support cannot stop at the school gate. Parents should be given guidance on recognising problems and supporting their children.
8. Promote mental health literacy among students, so that seeking help is seen as a sign of strength rather than something to be ashamed of.
Most importantly, we must move away from a situation where schools only respond when a crisis occurs. Prevention, early identification and early intervention must become the foundation of school mental health support.
The government should therefore consider developing a comprehensive National School Mental Health Framework with clear standards for staffing, referral, intervention, crisis response and collaboration between the education and health sectors.
Our children spend a significant part of their lives in school. If we want them to succeed academically, we must also ensure that they are emotionally and psychologically well.
Mental health support in schools is not an additional service or a luxury. It is an essential component of education and child development.
We must invest today in stronger school-based mental health services because protecting the mental wellbeing of our young people is ultimately an investment in the wellbeing and resilience of the nation.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Member of Mental Health Advisory Council

Title: Fauzi Omar: Sports' fearless pen
Article:
LETTERS:
There are sportswriters, and then there are rare voices who do more than report the game; they interpret its pulse, its conscience, and its disappointments. Datuk Fauzi Omar belongs to this category - a writer whose columns were not merely read, but awaited.
For those of us who grew up with the quiet thrill of opening a newspaper and searching for his name, Fauzi was a weekly lesson in clarity, courage, and conviction. He wrote with a sharpness that never felt performative, only purposeful. He called a spade a spade, never softened the blow, never hid behind polite ambiguity, and never insulted the intelligence of his readers. In a sporting culture too often addicted to clichés, he offered honesty. In a landscape crowded with noise, he gave us precision.
His writing carried the unmistakable stamp of a man who loved football deeply, especially Manchester United, but loved the truth of sport even more. He understood that sport was never only about winning or losing. It was about systems, structures, schooling, leadership, development, integrity, and the long consequences of neglect. That is why his commentary felt larger than match reports or post-match reactions. He wrote like someone trying to protect the future of Malaysian sport from its own bad habits.
According to a recent profile, Fauzi Omar was one of the influential sports journalists who helped shape the era of New Straits Times, Malay Mail, and Sports Mirror, and he quit writing sports in 2000 after 25 years in the field. In that same account, his final column said he was bowing out because he did not want to be part of the politicisation and corruption of sport. That alone tells you everything you need to know about the moral architecture of his journalism: he was never interested in easy applause. He was interested in what was right.
That is why his words still echo. He was developmental, but never gentle to the point of dilution. He was hard-hitting, but never cruel. He was frank, but never crass. That balance is the mark of a great writer, someone who can wound complacency without wounding dignity.
THE WRITER I ADMIRED
I first admired Datuk Fauzi Omar from my schooling days, when his columns felt like a signal flare. They were inspiring because they were alive with judgment, yet rooted in fairness. He wrote in a way that made a young reader believe sports journalism could be more than commentary; it could be service.
What made him unforgettable was not only the strength of his opinions, but the integrity behind them. He seemed to know instinctively that sport reflects a nation's habits. When our schools neglect games, when the pipeline is broken, when development is reduced to slogans, the damage goes far beyond the pitch. In a 2023 remembrance of Malaysia's sportswriting legends, Fauzi said the history of sport was "a rich tapestry of sporting life" and that sports journalism owed much to the athletes and officials of earlier eras. That sensibility, historical, humane, and unsentimental, is exactly what made his writing so enduring.
He sounded wry and disappointed at what is happening to Malaysian football. He spoke of the destroyed pipeline, the neglected school games, and the need to restore balance between education and sport. That is not nostalgia for its own sake; it is a warning. It is also a call to national responsibility.
MEETING THE MAN
Meeting Datuk Fauzi Omar for an early dinner hosted by Terence Fernandez was a genuine joy.
Terence wanted to meet up with the person who gave him his start in journalism 30 years ago when Fauzi was the editor of The Malay Mail.
There is something deeply moving about encountering a writer you have admired for decades and finding that the person is every bit as warm, respectful, and composed as the prose once suggested.
Looking trim and sharp even after seven decades, he carried himself with the elegance of someone who has never needed to announce his importance.
And that warmth matters. Because sometimes, the writers we admire most are remembered for their edge, their firmness, their fearless opinions – and yes, their ego. But Fauzi represents grace, the kind shown in his mannerisms, his gentle gestures, and the ease with which he relates to people even while speaking hard truths. And his bewilderment that people still remember him.
Encounters like these remind us that journalism is not only a profession; it is a lineage of relationships, memory, and shared values. To sit with men like Fauzi Omar is to be reminded that writing can still carry honour.
A NATIONAL SERVICE
Datuk Fauzi Omar's return to sports commentary would be monumental.
Malaysia still needs fearless writers who can speak plainly about not just what ails Malaysian sports - but what the remedy could be.
RAVINDRAN RAMAN KUTTY
LETTERS

Title: Seven Yemeni men investigated over dangerous stunts while celebrating friend's wedding
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seven Yemeni men, including five public university students, are being investigated after they were seen performing dangerous acts by leaning out of and sitting on the windows of two moving vehicles along Jalan Sungai Besi here.
City police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa confirmed the authenticity of a viral video on Threads showing the group engaging in dangerous acts involving the two vehicles.
He said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred about 12.30am yesterday when both vehicles were travelling along Jalan Sungai Besi towards Jalan Bukit Bintang.
"The passengers of both vehicles acted dangerously by leaning their bodies out of and sitting on the vehicle door windows while the vehicles were moving.
"The group involved comprised seven Yemeni men aged between 23 and 26. Five of them are public university students in Kedah, while the other two are university graduates," he said in a statement.
Zamzuri said questioning the drivers found that the acts were carried out for fun to celebrate a friend's wedding.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 336 of the Penal Code, which concerns negligent or rash acts that endanger the life or personal safety of others.
If convicted, the offence carries a jail term of up to three months, a fine of up to RM500, or both.
"Members of the public or witnesses with information on the incident are urged to assist the investigation by contacting the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station," he said.

Title: Gang violence, family killings among major crimes this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A suspected turf war between two gangs with alleged links to secret societies is emerging as a possible motive behind a brazen roadside attack in Taman Alam Megah, Shah Alam, which left one man dead and several others injured.
The incident, which occurred at about 2pm on Monday, unfolded in the middle of Jalan Mandolin 33/5, Section 28, after several men arrived at the scene in a number of vehicles.
A dashcam recording of the attack, which later went viral on social media, showed a group of men engaging in a violent confrontation on the road, with several individuals seen wielding and using sharp weapons.
One of the men died at the scene, while several others were injured. Police later said a blue multi-purpose vehicle was also seen crashing into one of the individuals during the incident.
The case triggered a major investigation after footage of the daylight violence began circulating online
Investigations have since taken a more significant turn, with Selangor police saying the violence is believed to have stemmed from hostility and a dispute over territorial rights between two gangs.
As of Wednesday, police had arrested 11 individuals, aged between their 20s and 30s.
Below are some of the other major crimes reported in the country this week:
Four members of family found dead in Desa ParkCity condo
A quiet residential area in Desa ParkCity, Kepong, was shaken on Thursday after four members of a family were found dead in and around their condominium unit.
Police were initially alerted after receiving a report that a 48-year-old man had fallen from the residential building.
A police team later went to the man's unit and, with the assistance of the Fire and Rescue Department, forced open the door.
Inside, they found the man's 47-year-old wife and their two children — a nine-year-old girl and a seven-year-old boy, dead in separate rooms.
Police said all three victims found inside the unit had suffered severe injuries to their necks. Police also recovered a knife believed to have been used in the incident.
It was later learnt that a love scam which allegedly left a family saddled with RM260,000 in losses and debts, was believed to have led to the murder of the woman and her two children.
Probe into Sunway Lagoon roller coaster incident widens
A roller coaster incident at Sunway Lagoon last Saturday left 10 visitors injured and prompted police and several technical agencies to investigate whether negligence or sabotage was involved.
The incident occurred at about 9pm and involved a roller coaster carrying 22 passengers, comprising local visitors and foreign tourists.
Ten of the passengers sought medical treatment following the incident, although no deaths were reported.
Sunway Theme Parks said it was cooperating fully with the relevant authorities and providing medical assistance and support to those affected.
By Wednesday, Selangor police said they were conducting a detailed investigation together with the Fire and Rescue Department and the Selangor Department of Occupational Safety and Health.
Police said investigators were examining whether there were elements of negligence or sabotage, with findings from the various agencies to be cross-checked to determine the actual cause of the incident.
The Selangor government is also awaiting the technical findings before determining the next course of action.
Policeman arrested for having affair with detainee's wife
Police have launched an internal investigation into a narcotics officer following allegations that he had an affair with the wife of a suspect who was earlier arrested for a drug-related offence.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the probe was initiated after a 30-second video clip purportedly involving the officer went viral on social media.
He said the officer's statement had been recorded and police would await the outcome of the internal investigation before deciding on further action.
The video showed more than 10 villagers, including a village head, gathered outside a house in Kuala Krai, with a car believed to belong to the officer parked outside.

Title: Ecuador ex-president convicted of corruption
Article:
QUITO: An Ecuadoran court on Friday convicted ex-president Lenin Moreno of accepting bribes from a Chinese company that built the country's biggest hydroelectric dam.
The Attorney General's office said that Moreno, who governed from 2017 to 2021, was among four people convicted in the case involving the construction of the Coca Codo Sinclair dam by China's Sinohydro.
Moreno was vice-president under socialist president Rafael Correa at the time of the alleged corruption, between 2007 and 2013.
He succeeded Correa, with the latter's backing, but later fell out with his mentor by shifting to the right and aligning himself more closely with the United States.
The court in Quito has not yet sentenced him.
Moreno remains free pending his sentencing.
Prosecutors have asked for him to receive a six-and-a-half-year prison term.
The 73-year-old paraplegic, who served as the United Nations special envoy on disability issues, insisted Friday after the ruling that he had never received "a single cent" from Sinohydro.
He blamed the case on "the Correa regime," saying his former-backer-turned-rival, who has also been convicted of corruption but is exiled in Belgium, "promised to take revenge on me."
Prosecutors say Sinohydro paid bribes totaling $76 million, around four percent of the cost of the hydroelectric project.
Three other Ecuadoran nationals were convicted alongside Moreno, including two former managers of the power plant.
Around 20 people have been implicated in the case in total, including Moreno's wife, his daughter, businesspeople, and a former Chinese ambassador to Quito.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Study proposed to identify pollution sources in Hulu Perak
Article:
IPOH: The Department of Environment (DOE) is proposing a total maximum daily load (TMDL) study for Hulu Perak to identify and map potential sources contributing to elevated mineral levels in Sungai Rui.
Perak DOE senior environmental control officer S. Pravin said the study would provide the state government with technical data needed to make informed decisions and strengthen measures to control pollution at its source.
"Since a management board has been established under the Perak government, we have proposed a TMDL study for Hulu Perak.
"Through the study, we can map all the sources along the river, not just mining activities, and identify the agencies responsible," he said.
Pravin said DOE had briefed the Perak Water Resources Management Board on the proposal, with the agency expected to prepare a working paper to secure funding for the study.
He said the need for a more comprehensive assessment was underscored by similar incidents recorded in 2018 and 2019.
"There may have been similar incidents before, but they were not well documented. Now, with the recent report, we have better findings.
"We are not trying to deny the source because the source does exist. What we need is technical data so the state government can make the right decisions to control the issue in the future."
On the recent blue water phenomenon, Pravin said DOE sampling found relatively high copper levels at several locations along Sungai Rui, rather than being confined to the area where Rahman Hydraulic Tin Sdn Bhd (RHT) was operating.
He attributed the elevated readings, among other factors, to unusually heavy rainfall in the second week of October last year, which could have washed minerals from exposed areas into the river.
"Normally, heavy rainfall would be around 30mm at most, but during that week, it reached 90mm.
[[nid:1521081]]
"There may have been significant washdown of minerals, not only from RHT but also from surrounding areas. Individual mining activities could also have contributed to the washdown."
Pravin also gave an assurance that loma fish from the area remained safe for consumption, with current findings showing mineral levels within permissible limits.
"Technically, the loma fish are still safe to eat because the levels are within safe limits. If they were not safe, I don't think we would allow people to eat them."
He said DOE monitoring also showed that identified sources remained under control.
Pravin said large-scale mining activities had been subject to Environmental Impact Assessment requirements since 2015, with projects under the Second Schedule requiring public display and opportunities for objections and feedback.
He said the process allowed mitigation measures to be identified and implemented before mining activities proceeded.
Meanwhile, Pravin said the existing water treatment plant had been properly provided for and was currently undergoing repairs and flushing works.
He added that any new mining proposals in Hulu Perak should undergo a comprehensive assessment to ensure the combined effects of activities in the area were properly evaluated.
"Perhaps a cumulative study should also be carried out."

Title: Number of missing in deadly Nepal, China floods jumps past 2,400
Article:
NUWAKOT: The number of people missing in Nepal and China surpassed 2,400 Friday, underscoring the scale of the disaster days after a tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept away villages and killed hundreds.
Rescuers were battling through mud even as the threat of new floods loomed, with emergency teams recovering 586 bodies so far – and some of the dead swept downstream as far away as India.
The new figures came as Nepal's disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing persons list already including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash.
Relatives have crowded hospitals in Nepal's capital in a painful hunt for their loved ones, with posters on the walls bearing photos and names of the missing.
"Today is the third day and we don't know anything. Hopefully he is in a safe place," Samjhana Thing, 27, told AFP referring to her brother. "We lost everything. He is our everything."
The US Geological Survey said the disaster – the deadliest for Nepal since a 2015 earthquake – was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.
The deluge of ice and mud also caused huge lakes to form, and one of these formations has become a direct threat to emergency workers scouring the region for survivors.
Nepali police urged all rescuers to "immediately move to a safe location", saying it had received information that "a water dam has burst again on the Tibetan side."
In Tibet, China was forced to suspend its rescue operation at the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of renewed flooding on Friday, before saying the threat had eased.
State broadcaster CCTV reported that a lake formed by immense piles of debris began overflowing toward where rescue teams were headed, but later said the water level of the pool had dropped.
Rescue operations were therefore "proceeding in an orderly manner", it added.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, who chaired a meeting on rescue efforts, offered Beijing's help to Nepal's emergency operations.
'ALL SWEPT AWAY'
Emergency teams had been racing to retrieve survivors from affected zones, where the widespread devastation meant food and water supplies were running out.
The Nepali military located people trapped in the tunnel of Trishuli 3A hydropower project, where they were working to find a way in to extract the survivors.
"Two helicopters have been dispatched but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel," army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.
Some 350 workers and residents have been brought to safety from the site, he added, but efforts were ongoing to rescue more than 100 people trapped in the same area.
Workers rescued from other dam projects along the Trishuli valley described a disaster that unfolded with terrifying speed.
Buddha Tamang told AFP he survived only because he was inside a tunnel at the dam where he worked when the flood struck.
"The senior officers working on the other side, they were all swept away," Tamang, who was airlifted on Thursday after being marooned for more than 24 hours, told AFP.
'I JUST WANT MY SON BACK'
Survivors in a makeshift Nepali hospital endured an agonising wait for news of their missing loved ones.
Kula Priya, whose eldest son is missing, said she had lost everything when the wave of mud and water swept in.
"I don't care for wealth. I just want my son back. If any of you could rescue my son, please do it for me," she told AFP.
Nepal reported a death toll of 579 people on Friday.
There are 1,924 people, including 517 foreigners, who are out of contact in Nepal, the disaster authority said. The previous missing figure was 977.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.
Across the border in Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and where the only sources of information are Chinese authorities – seven have died and 554 remain missing, the state Xinhua news agency reported early Saturday.
Authorities also said they had evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet.
PILGRIMAGE ROUTE
Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among those missing on the border, as many were on a pilgrimage to Tibet's Mount Kailash.
Sivaranjani Muthunathan was travelling by bus with 56 others towards the Chinese border when they became stuck in what they thought was a traffic jam.
"Then there was fog, smoke, something that seemed to suddenly engulf us," Muthunathan, 46, told AFP on Friday, showing a phone video she recorded of a torrent surging towards her.
Around them, vehicles were swept away or buried under mud.
"One by one, we also climbed out through the driver's side," then scrambled up a hill, she said.

Title: Three ex-PMs, a former minister and landmark rulings: A week in Malaysia's courts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It was a week when Malaysia's courts were dominated by familiar political faces, major corruption cases and closely watched rulings.
The most striking scene came on Thursday, when three former prime ministers - Datuk Seri Najib Razak, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob - were at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex at the same time.
All three were there for separate proceedings, turning the sprawling court complex into an unusually crowded focal point for reporters, photographers, lawyers and political supporters.
Najib was attending proceedings in the US$5.64 billion 1Malaysia Development Bhd civil suit, while Muhyiddin was in court for his Jana Wibawa corruption and money-laundering trial.
Ismail Sabri, meanwhile, appeared before the Sessions Court to face a charge of failing to declare assets, capping a week that also saw another former minister charged and several major criminal, civil and public-interest cases return to the spotlight.
Below are some of the major court cases this week:
Saravanan charged over RM1.097 million in bribes
Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan was charged with three counts of receiving RM1.097 million in bribes linked to the approval of foreign worker quotas.
The MIC deputy president's court appearance came with its own drama as about 100 supporters gathered outside the Jalan Duta Court Complex in a show of solidarity.
The atmosphere briefly turned tense when several supporters complained that they were being prevented from entering.
Saravanan arrived to cheers and chants of "Hidup Datuk Seri!" from supporters before making his way into court.
The 58-year-old politician pleaded not guilty to the three counts and was released on a RM450,000 bail which was paid by a friend.
Indira Gandhi loses RM100 million suit appeal
The Court of Appeal this week dismissed M. Indira Gandhi's appeal in her RM100 million suit against the police and government over their failure to locate her former husband and to reunite her with her youngest daughter.
A three-member bench chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan ruled that Indira had failed to prove that shortcomings by the police directly caused her loss.
Datuk Faizah Jamaludin, who delivered the unanimous decision, said Indira had to establish that, but for the alleged omissions, her former husband K. Pathmanathan would probably have been arrested or her daughter Prasana Diksa found.
The court nevertheless highlighted shortcomings in efforts to execute the arrest warrant and recover the child.
Defence closes case in Bandar Utama school stabbing case
The defence closed its case this week in the murder trial of a 15-year-old boy accused of fatally stabbing his 16-year-old schoolmate at a secondary school in Bandar Utama last year.
The case heard evidence from students, teachers, the victim's mother, a pathologist and a senior investigating officer.
The defence, meanwhile, called two witnesses namely the teenager himself and Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta consultant forensic psychiatrist Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony.
The teenager chose to give an unsworn statement from the dock and expressed remorse over the death of his schoolmate, while the defence relied on psychiatric evidence to support its plea of unsoundness of mind.
Drama at Zara Qairina inquest
In Kota Kinabalu, the inquest into the death of 13-year-old schoolgirl Zara Qairina Mahathir produced one of the week's most dramatic courtroom moments.
Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan suddenly stood and left the bench after twice asking, "Am I not fair enough?" during the questioning of consultant psychiatrist Dr Wong Haw Huo.
The exchange began when lawyer Datuk Ram Singh, representing one of the teenagers charged in the bullying case involving Zara Qairina, repeatedly pressed Wong to give direct answers about the teenager's fall and whether she had been alone before the incident.
A lawyer representing Zara Qairina's mother then remarked that Ram's questioning appeared harsh, prompting an exchange over fairness before the coroner left the courtroom. Proceedings were halted for about 50 minutes.
When proceedings resumed, Ram apologised and said he had not intended to question the court's fairness. Amir Shah also apologised, saying it was the first time in his 21 years of service that he had walked out from the bench, and reminded those involved to remain professional and not become emotional.
Rape sentence cut from 10 years to one
The Kuantan High Court made headlines after reducing a man's jail sentence for statutory rape from 10 years to one year.
The court cited, among others, his youth and prospects for rehabilitation in allowing the sentencing appeal.
The substantial reduction in sentence made the case one of the week's more closely watched criminal appeals.
Negri Sembilan govt fails in bid against two Undang
In Seremban, the High Court dismissed two applications by the state government seeking the immediate eviction of the Undang of Rembau and the Undang of Sungei Ujong from their official halls and residences.
Judge Roz Mawar Rozain ruled that the state government lacked locus standi to bring the proceedings as the action should have been instituted by the State director of Lands and Mines, as required under Section 16 of the National Land Code.
The court found that the state government had failed to establish either registered ownership of the premises or a right to possession sufficient to sustain the eviction applications.
The state government was also ordered to pay RM25,000 each to Abdul Rahim Yasin and Datuk Mubarak Thahak, bringing the total costs to RM50,000.
Aman Palestin beats RM21 million forfeiture bid
The Shah Alam High Court dismissed the prosecution's bid to forfeit more than RM21 million in assets belonging to Aman Palestin, including funds in 12 bank accounts, US$139,650.68 in foreign currency and a one-kilogramme gold bar.
Judge Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar ruled that the prosecution had failed to prove that the money and gold bar were the subject matter of an offence or proceeds of unlawful activities.
The case stems from investigations involving Aman Palestin's funds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Norwegians mourn King Harald as son succeeds to throne
Article:
OSLO: Hugging and laying flowers, thousands of people gathered in Oslo on Friday to pay their respects to Norway's King Harald, who died Friday aged 89 after a reign of three and a half decades.
Harald's 53-year-old son immediately succeeded him on the throne as King Haakon VIII. He takes over a monarchy hailed for its modernity and modesty, but beset by a string of scandals in recent years.
"An era has ended. A new one begins. The king is dead. Long live the king," Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said in a speech shortly after meeting the new monarch.
"We will remember King Harald for his love for his people, for his humour and warmth, and for his unwavering faith in us."
A motor procession brought King Harald's casket from Oslo University Hospital to the royal palace on Friday evening as wellwishers lined the streets.
Haakon arrived at the palace earlier with his 22-year-old daughter Ingrid Alexandra – the new crown princess – to formally inform the government of his father's death.
In a statement, Haakon thanked "the government and Norwegian people for their support and sympathy for the Royal Family at this time."
Norway's parliament said the new monarch would take an oath of allegiance in its main chamber on September 1.
The government announced a period of national mourning until Harald's funeral, the date of which is yet to be set.
'LIKE A GRANDFATHER'
Europe's oldest reigning monarch, King Harald had been in hospital in Oslo since August 17, suffering from haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells that leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
Store said Harald, who ascended to the throne in 1991, was "a king of his time and for his time."
He said Harald accompanied Norway through decades of enormous change during which the country "grew richer, we became more numerous, and we became more diverse."
Thousands of Norwegians massed outside the palace in Oslo throughout the day and even as heavy rains started pouring down in the evening.
[[nid:1521027]]
They laid down mountains of flowers, cards and red, white and blue national flags, and many hugged and held each other.
"He has meant a great deal, he has been a unifying king, he has been a king of the people," Line Stousland, 49, told AFP, before going to lay down a bouquet of flowers.
She added that he had been "like a grandfather to the whole nation."
Harald was widely seen as the embodiment of an open and tolerant Norway.
"I really have to mention all the speeches he has given over the years, which have meant a lot to Norway, both in difficult times and also when there have been events to celebrate," 37-year-old Martin Korslund, who arrived at the palace Friday evening, told AFP.
Many of those AFP spoke with pointed in particular to Harald's speech after one of the country's biggest recent traumas – a devastating massacre in 2011.
Neo-Nazi Anders Behring Breivik killed 77 people in twin attacks, in Norway's worst massacre since World War II.
Harald "was someone who always seemed to find the words that brought us together and gave us a sense of security," Caroline Vagle, a reporter for magazine Se og Hor, told AFP.
Tributes poured in from leaders around the world, including those of France, Germany, India, Israel, Italy, Jordan and Ukraine, as well as the royal houses of Europe.
TURBULENT YEAR
Harald faced mounting health problems in his final years, forcing him to scale back his official schedule.
But he ruled out abdicating, arguing that he took a lifelong oath before the Norwegian parliament.
The past year has been a turbulent one for the Norwegian royal family.
Harald's wife Queen Sonja, also 89, was briefly admitted to hospital in May due to heart problems.
Haakon's wife Mette-Marit is under scrutiny for her ties to the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
In June, Mette-Marit's son from a relationship prior to her marriage to Haakon, Marius Borg Hoiby, was sentenced to four years in prison for two rapes.
Suffering herself from a serious lung disease, Mette-Marit, 53, underwent a lung transplant in July.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JMG: No compromise on Hulu Perak mining violations
Article:
IPOH: The Perak Mineral and Geoscience Department (JMG) is taking a no-compromise approach towards mining violations in Hulu Perak, with three operators having had their operations suspended since last year for failing to comply with the requirements.
Its director Nizarulikram Abdul Rahim said the department would continue to take enforcement action against operators found breaching conditions, particularly those involving wastewater, surface run-off and effluent discharge.
He said mining activities were subject to strict regulations under the Mineral Development Act 1994, with operators required to ensure wastewater was properly managed and treated before any discharge.
"Basically, a mine cannot simply discharge water. It must be kept within a closed circuit, meaning the water is reused.
"If the water needs to be discharged for certain reasons, it must first be treated," he said.
Nizarulikram said mine wastewater generally had a low pH and could contain high levels of metals, making proper treatment essential under the Mineral Development (Effluent) Regulations 2016.
He said JMG's firm enforcement stance was reflected in its latest action against Rahman Hydraulic Tin Sdn Bhd (RHT), whose operations were ordered to be suspended temporarily from Aug 12 following the detection of acidic water discharge from Detention Ponds 4 and 5.
The water recorded pH readings ranging from 2.29 to 2.33.
The action followed an inspection conducted after heavy rain on Aug 3, when about 60mm of rainfall was recorded within an hour, exceeding the maximum design intensity of 50mm for RHT's existing drainage and detention pond system.
"When JMG conducted a visit there, we found that untreated water had been discharged into the river.
"So, we stopped their operations temporarily until they submit a mitigation proposal. Once we are satisfied, we will consider allowing them to resume operations," said Nizarulikram.
He said JMG had previously issued several directives to RHT covering run-off management, erosion control and maintenance of its tailings ponds.
The company was also required to include total suspended solids and conductivity readings in its daily reports to enable closer monitoring of water quality.
Nizarulikram said RHT was further directed to carry out lime dosing away from the river to ensure that water was properly treated before being discharged, if necessary.
He said JMG's enforcement was not limited to RHT, with its records showing that RHT, MCRE Resources Sdn Bhd and Nalidah Tin Mine Sdn Bhd had previously been ordered to suspend their operations for three weeks last November, subject to pollution-control mitigation measures.
[[nid:1521062]]
The suspension involving MCRE Resources was extended in December following non-compliance with conditions under its Environmental Impact Assessment and a Stop Work Order issued by the Department of Environment (DOE).
Its operations were subsequently allowed to resume in January after the Stop Work Order was withdrawn.
Nizarulikram said the enforcement actions demonstrated that mining operators could not take regulatory and environmental requirements lightly.
He said operators were expected to ensure their activities complied with all conditions imposed, particularly those relating to water management and pollution prevention.
"We will continue to monitor. If there is non-compliance, action will be taken."
Nizarulikram, however, said RHT's latest suspension should not be taken as proof that the mining operation was responsible for the recent bluish discolouration of Sungai Perak.
He said the suspension was imposed specifically over detected non-compliance and did not, by itself, establish a link between the operation and the river's colour change.
"The cause of the phenomenon needs to be determined based on the overall evidence, including the location and timing of the incident, flow patterns, water sampling and water quality analysis," he said.
He said RHT's suspension would remain until the operator submitted a mitigation proposal and JMG was satisfied with the measures proposed.
"It is up to RHT to submit the proposal to us. If they want to resume operations quickly, they should submit it as soon as possible."
Nizarulikram said JMG would continue with routine monitoring and surprise inspections to ensure mining operators complied with the conditions imposed on their operations.
He said operators were also required to provide relevant operational and environmental data to JMG as part of ongoing monitoring.

Title: Hizbollah chief again rejects Lebanon-Israel deal, refuses 'surrender'
Article:
BEIRUT: Hizbollah chief Naim Qassem on Friday again rejected a deal struck between Israel and Lebanon and said his Iran-backed group refused to "surrender" nearly six months after war erupted with Israel.
"We are against the framework agreement and call for its downfall," Qassem said in a televised address broadcast on the group's Al-Manar television channel.
Israel and Lebanon launched US-sponsored direct talks after Hizbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war on March 2 by attacking Israel, which responded with massive strikes and a ground invasion that Lebanese authorities say have killed more than 4,300 people.
At talks in late June, Lebanon and Israel signed a framework deal that calls for the disarmament of Hizbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region, starting in "pilot zones."
"The framework agreement is illegitimate, unlawful, humiliating, destructive to Lebanese sovereignty," Qassem said.
"We do not agree to the 'pilot zones' or to what comes from them," he said, also rejecting any proposed verification system.
After talks in Rome earlier this month, a Lebanese source told AFP that agreement was reached on a "shortlist" of countries that might oversee the implementation of the pilot zone process, namely the Lebanese army's dismantlement of any Hizbollah infrastructure in the areas.
A fresh round of talks had been planned for early September, but no date has been announced yet.
Although violence has dropped since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding on the broader conflict in June and the Israel-Lebanon framework agreement later that month, Lebanon still reports regular Israeli strikes, artillery shelling and broad demolitions of civilian buildings in southern villages and towns.
Israeli forces are operating inside a self-declared "security zone", which runs around 10 kilometres (six miles) deep inside Lebanese territory along the border.
Lebanon's state-run National News Agency on Friday reported several Israeli airstrikes in the country's south including on the Nabatieh area, where it has increased attacks in recent days.
Qassem said his group supported the implementation of a November 2024 ceasefire that sought to end a previous war with Israel.
"We will keep our heads high and we will not surrender," he vowed.

Title: Trump to mark 9/11 at Pentagon, not New York
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday he would mark the 25th anniversary of the Sept 11, 2001, attacks at the Pentagon – but angrily denied skipping a memorial in New York because of a row over a speech.
The New York Times reported that Trump originally intended to commemorate the day with remarks at the site of the Twin Towers but changed his plans because the memorial's organisers do not allow speeches.
Asked by reporters why he was not going to New York for the anniversary, Trump replied: "Because I'm going to the Pentagon."
When asked why he could not attend both locations, Trump repeated his answer.
The 9/11 attacks killed nearly 3,000 people.
Hijackers from the Al-Qaeda network crashed two airliners into the Twin Towers in New York and a third into the Pentagon near Washington, while a fourth plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after a revolt by the passengers.
The White House told AFP that Vice President JD Vance was "still traveling" to New York and said that "all three sites will be represented with administration officials in attendance."
"On the 25th anniversary of this tragic day, the President will remember those who were killed at the hands of evil terrorists, honor their loved ones, and pay tribute to the brave first responders who put their lives on the line to rescue their fellow Americans," White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said in a statement.
The Pentagon declined to comment.
Trump had earlier issued a lengthy social media post slamming The New York Times report, with a harsh, renewed attack on one of its journalists, Maggie Haberman, whom he called "Maggot Hagerman."
"This is more Corrupt News, I've been to New York many times over the years, and no one ever speaks, it's a 'solemn ceremony!'" Trump said on his Truth Social network.
"I never even thought of what Maggot made up, and besides, I would love not to speak, because I'm speaking all the time, and this is a day to remember the victims, and their beautiful family members."

Title: Called a ‘gambling boss’, Anwar fires back: I cut special lottery draws from 22 to eight
Article:
