KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hit back at critics branding him a “
tauke judi
”, or gambling boss, saying his government had instead cut the number of special lottery draws from 22 a year to eight.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the reduction showed his administration had taken steps to curb gaming activities.
“You held 22 special draws, but I reduced it to eight. Is it enough? No. But why am I being insulted for this?
“Before you attack me, you should look at yourself in the mirror first,” he said at the launch of the
Skim Usahawan Bangkit Permatang Pauh
in Penanti today.
The number of special lottery draws had been increased from eight to 22 a year under administrations between 2020 and 2022, before Anwar’s government reduced it to eight.
His remarks appeared to be in response to recent criticism from Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor after the Federal Court dismissed the state government’s bid to overturn a ruling preventing it from refusing to renew licences for pool betting and lottery operators.
The case stemmed from Kedah’s move to effectively end licensed gambling in the state by refusing to renew the operators’ business licences.
Sanusi said the decision on whether gambling activities would be allowed in Kedah now rested with Anwar.
He also warned that Kedahans would “curse” the prime minister if gambling activities were allowed to resume in the state.

Title: Sarawak targets 20,000 affordable homes by 2030, says deputy minister
Article:
SIBU, Aug 29 — The Sarawak government will continue working with the housing industry to meet the people’s housing needs, including its target of building 20,000 affordable homes by 2030.
State Deputy Minister of Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang said collaboration with industry players remained important in ensuring housing was suitable, of good quality and responsive to the needs of Sarawakians.
“The state government will continue to work with the industry to ensure the rakyat’s housing needs are met, including the building of 20,000 affordable housings by 2030.
“Where there are challenges, let us discuss them. Where there are opportunities, let us work together. And where improvements are needed, let us find practical solutions together,” he said when officiating at Sarawak Housing Real Estate Developers Association (Sheda) Home and Property Roadshow 2026 at Wisma Sanyan here yesterday.
The Pelawan assemblyman said the government was aware of its role to ensure every Sarawakian had a proper roof over their head, adding that cooperation with government-linked companies, statutory bodies and private developers remained important in expanding access to housing.
He also highlighted the Housing Deposit and Repayment Assistance Scheme (HDRAS), which assists eligible first-time homebuyers, particularly those in the B40 and M40 income groups, in overcoming financial barriers to home ownership.
Under HDRAS, eligible applicants may receive assistance of up to RM10,000 towards their housing deposit or, where applicable, RM200 a month towards their housing loan repayment for up to 48 months.
Tiang said 1,206 recipients benefitted from the scheme last year, involving RM12.06 million in assistance, while another 387 recipients had benefitted as of July this year.
“This momentum will continue at the Sheda Property Expo 2026, where we will witness the presentation of mock cheques to 20 recipients, amounting to a total assistance of RM200,000.
“This is a meaningful part of the expo because it reminds us that behind every housing policy and every housing programme, there are real individuals and families whose lives can be positively impacted,” he said.
In his remarks, Sheda Sibu branch chairman Wong Siong Nee said house prices were expected to rise next year due to higher construction material and transportation costs, compounded by a shortage of local workers.
Meanwhile, Tiang called on the federal government to review the new stamp duty policy on property development agreements, which could impose a heavy upfront financial burden on Sarawak developers and potentially slow housing development in the state.
According to him, developers undertaking projects through joint ventures are required to pay stamp duty based on the value of the developed land, at rates ranging from one to four per cent.
“In the past, when a developer signed a development agreement and power of attorney with a landowner to jointly develop the land, only a flat-rate stamp duty of RM10 was normally imposed on both documents.
“However, under the new policy issued by the federal government, developers are now required to pay stamp duty twice based on the value of the land, even before the actual development process begins, despite the land being owned by the landowner rather than the developer.
“I urge the federal government to review this policy because the situation in Sarawak is different from that in Peninsular Malaysia.”
Tiang pointed out that many developers in Sarawak were actually property developers rather than landowners, unlike in Peninsular Malaysia, where developers would typically purchase and own the land.
He also stressed that signing a joint-venture agreement did not mean a project would automatically proceed, as developers still had to obtain planning approval and fulfil other regulatory requirements.
He also pointed out that Sarawak developers already faced higher costs in areas such as logistics and building materials.
“But that does not mean we should stop looking for ways and solutions to overcome these challenges. I believe that through continued dialogue with Sheda, which has been very proactive, we can work together to find practical solutions,” he added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Police arrest two men for allegedly impersonating enforcement officers to extort RM1,500 from foreigner in Penampang
Article:
PENAMPANG, Aug 29 — Police have arrested two local men for allegedly posing as enforcement officers and attempting to extort RM1,500 from a foreign national at Kampung Koidupan Sugud here early yesterday.
Penampang district police chief Supt Sammy Newton said the incident occurred at about 12.10am when the suspects, aged 19 and 28, allegedly approached the victim wearing attire resembling enforcement agency uniforms and demanded to see his identification documents.
The suspects then allegedly accused the victim of committing an offence for failing to produce his passport and demanded RM1,500 to settle the matter.
However, their alleged scheme was uncovered when the victim asked them to produce their authority cards.
“The suspects suddenly attempted to flee but were detained by villagers before being handed over to police,” Sammy said in a statement.
Police also seized several pieces of clothing resembling enforcement agency uniforms, which are believed to have been worn by the suspects during the incident.
The case is being investigated under Sections 384 and 170 of the Penal Code for alleged extortion and impersonating a public servant.
Sammy urged the public to remain vigilant when approached by individuals claiming to be enforcement officers.
“Any suspicious incident or behaviour should be reported to police immediately,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Water disruption expected as Sarawak Water conducts Jalan Matang pipeline repairs Sept 4-5; traffic diversion from Sept 3-12
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 29 — Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd (Sarawak Water) will carry out planned repair works on a 1,100mm-diameter water pipeline along Jalan Matang here from 10pm on September 4 to noon on September 5.
The utility company said the works followed technical investigations and assessments of a suspected leak in the pipeline, which is located along the road median.
“The repair is being undertaken to address the issue in a controlled manner and to reduce the risk of a more serious unplanned disruption to water supply,” it said in a statement.
The pipeline is one of Sarawak Water’s main pipelines supplying treated water to the Bukit Siol Reservoir, which serves consumers in Kuching, Petra Jaya and surrounding areas.
Sarawak Water said extensive preparation was required due to the pipeline’s location in the road median and restricted working space. This includes excavation, providing access for heavy machinery, draining water from the pipeline, traffic management and implementing safety measures.
It added that coordination was also being carried out with relevant agencies and utility providers to ensure the works could be completed safely and as scheduled.
During the repair, consumers in affected areas may experience low water pressure or temporary disruption to their water supply.
Consumers are advised to store sufficient water for at least 24 hours of essential use before the works begin as a precaution, particularly in case of delays caused by unforeseen technical issues or site conditions.
Sarawak Water said contingency measures had been put in place, including the mobilisation of water tankers to affected areas, with priority given to critical facilities and essential needs.
“Once the repair works are completed, water supply will be restored gradually. Water pressure may take some time to return to normal.
“Consumers in higher-elevated areas and locations further from the main distribution system may experience a longer recovery period.
“Consumers may also experience temporary discoloured water during the recovery period. Sarawak Water will carry out flushing works to restore water quality to normal,” it said.
Meanwhile, a temporary traffic diversion will be implemented from September 3 to 12 to facilitate site preparation, repair works and road reinstatement.
Affected traffic will be diverted via Jalan Matang Bersinar and Jalan Matang Bersinar 3.
Motorists are advised to follow temporary traffic signs and instructions, exercise caution when approaching the work area and plan their journeys accordingly.
“These works are necessary to safeguard the reliability of the important water supply main, and Sarawak Water teams will work continuously to complete the repair safely and restore water supply as quickly as possible,” Sarawak Water said.
Progress updates, including the commencement of works, completion of repairs and restoration of water supply, will be communicated through Sarawak Water’s official communication channels. — The Borneo Post

Title: Govt monitoring inflation to avoid cost pressure on the people amid West Asia crisis, says deputy minister
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 29 — The government is monitoring inflation movements due to developments in the West Asian crisis to ensure cost pressures from supply disruptions and rising commodity prices do not burden the people.
Deputy Economy Minister Datuk Seri Mohd Shahar Abdullah said the monitoring is important because developments in West Asia are changing rapidly and can potentially impact global supply chains and commodity prices.
He said the government is also ensuring the country’s supply, especially for strategic commodities such as oil, remains sufficient until the end of the year while taking appropriate measures to mitigate the crisis’s impact on the domestic economy.
“Right now, the aim is to ensure the country’s supply is guaranteed until year-end. That is the most important thing, and that is why we continuously observe and monitor from various angles.
“Not only are we looking at the oil supply for us to last until the end of the year, but we are also monitoring the movement of inflation on goods so that the pressure on the community is not felt as a whole,” he told reporters after officiating at the annual general meeting of the Malay Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKMM) Kelantan chapter, here last night.
Mohd Shahar said the government has yet to determine whether the situation in West Asia will improve or worsen, given developments in the conflict are difficult to predict.
He said that the government is not just waiting for the crisis to subside but is always prepared to face various possibilities to ensure the country’s economy remains resilient.
“We are monitoring daily, and we have a Crisis Monitoring Dashboard. We also communicate with the people through that dashboard, which provides detailed information on what has happened.
“This situation is changing very rapidly. Whatever we do, it is to ensure our economy is resilient and to ensure that any initiatives taken are appropriate for the people,” he said.
According to Mohd Shahar, the current economic performance, which has recorded better-than-expected growth, should not make the government feel complacent; instead, monitoring and engagement with various parties should continue.
He added that this approach is important to ensure that any external pressure can be addressed immediately without causing excessive impact on the people or the domestic economy. — Bernama

Title: Sabah clam hunter survives crocodile attack after friend beats nine-foot reptile on the head
Article:
BEAUFORT, Aug 29 — A man was injured after being attacked and bitten by a crocodile while searching for clams in Sungai Siungau, near Kampung Lubok Weston, Thursday.
Hamdan Samad suffered injuries to his left leg and right hand in the 4pm incident. Kampung Weston Village Chief Masri Latif, when contacted by the
Daily Express
yesterday, said the victim was taken to hospital for treatment.
He said Hamdan and his friend, Ag Sabtu Omar, had just got out of their boat to search for clams when they encountered a crocodile estimated to be about nine feet long.
“The crocodile suddenly attacked him and he struggled with the reptile,” Masri said.
Fortunately, Ag Sabtu came to Hamdan’s aid and managed to free him by hitting the crocodile on the head until it released its grip.
After escaping, Hamdan realised he had suffered bite injuries to his hand and leg. He left the river and was taken to the Weston Health Clinic before being referred to Beaufort District Hospital.
Masri urged residents, especially fishermen and anglers, to be extra cautious when carrying out activities along the river, saying crocodile sightings in the area were becoming increasingly common.
He said there was more than one crocodile in the river and called for action to address the threat posed by the reptiles.
Masri said he had contacted the Wildlife Department about the incident and was informed that efforts would be made to trap the crocodile.
A similar incident involving a woman searching for clams in the river was reported several years ago. The woman survived after her companion fought off the crocodile. — Daily Express

Title: Kota Belud car wash crash sparks deja vu weeks after Kota Kinabalu International Airport smash
Article:
KOTA BELUD, Aug 29 — In a scene reminiscent of another that brought down a glass door at the Kota Kinabalu International Airport earlier this month, a 61-year-old driver lost control of her Perodua Ativa and crashed into a Perodua Alza and car wash along Jalan Raya, Thursday.
Kota Belud District Police Chief Supt Khairul Shah Peri said the incident occurred at 9.30am after the woman had finished using the automatic car wash.
“Initial investigations found that the driver lost control of her vehicle after exiting the automatic car wash machine,” he said in a statement yesterday.
The Ativa then veered off and crashed into the Alza parked nearby before hitting the iron structure of the automatic car wash.
The impact damaged the structure, while both vehicles were also involved in the accident. However, the woman was not injured.
The case is being investigated under Regulation 10 of the Road Traffic Rules 1959 (LN 166/59).
In the incident at KKIA on August 7, a 66-year-old woman suffered minor injuries after the SUV she was driving crashed into the Level 3 departure hall area.
The incident was believed to have occurred after the woman forgot to engage the vehicle’s “P” gear, causing it to move slowly.
She reportedly panicked and stepped on the accelerator, causing the vehicle to surge forward and crash into the building.
The driver managed to get out of the vehicle before the collision but suffered minor facial injuries from flying glass shards.
Police advised motorists to remain cautious while driving, ensure their vehicles are in good condition and comply with all traffic laws and regulations to avoid accidents. — Daily Express

Title: Perak mulls RM500 first‑time marriage incentive to ease financial burden on youths ahead of 2027 state budget
Article:
IPOH, Aug 29 — A proposal to introduce a RM500 First-Time Marriage Incentive for youths in Perak will be submitted to the relevant State Executive Council (Exco) member for further discussion and refinement before being considered under the 2027 state budget.
Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said the motion proposing the special incentive was unanimously approved during the recent fifth sitting of the Perak Youth Assembly.
He said the proposal reflected the state government’s concern and commitment to helping ease the financial burden faced by young people entering marriage.
“We view this as a positive initiative that demonstrates the state government’s care and concern by providing some assistance to newly married couples,” he told reporters after representing Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad at the presentation of the state-level National Youth Premier Award and the State Youth Special Award 2026 here last night.
Khairudin said the proposed assistance would target youths aged between 15 and 35, in line with the definition of youth under the Youth Development and Sports Act 2007 (Act 668).
He added that specific eligibility criteria would also be established, including that applicants must be Perak natives or have resided in the state for at least 10 years.
However, he said the final details and implementation of the proposed incentive would be subject to deliberation and approval by the State Executive Council before any official announcement is made.
“The proposal is expected to be finalised ahead of the presentation of the state budget in November,” he said.
Meanwhile, Khairudin said the National Premier Youth Award featured three categories, namely male individual, female individual and youth organisation, while the State Special Youth Award comprised seven categories fully funded by the state government.
“I hope the winners tonight will serve as a source of inspiration and motivation for young people, particularly youths in Perak, to become actively involved in youth organisations and, in the process, develop leadership qualities, skills, a spirit of volunteerism and integrity,” he said.
Khairudin said all recipients underwent a comprehensive assessment by an independent panel comprising youth development experts and former state youth leaders.
Winners of both the National Premier Youth Award and the State Special Youth Award received trophies and certificates, along with cash prizes ranging from RM1,000 to RM10,000, depending on their placing in their respective categories.
In the male individual category of the State-level National Premier Youth Award, Muhammad Amizan Lokman, 28, representing Hulu Perak, emerged as the winner, followed by Muhammad Saiful Hanif Khairi, 29, representing Muallim, as runner-up, and Muhammad Awliya Mohd Fauzi, 25, representing Kerian, in third place.
In the female individual category, M. Ashhwina, 20, representing Larut Matang, took first place, followed by C. Vhainmathy, 21, representing Kerian, as runner-up, and Nicole Tiuk Yu Xuan, 20, representing Hilir Perak, in third place.
Meanwhile, the Larut Matang District Youth Council emerged as the winner in the youth organisation category, followed by the Federation of Malay Students of the Peninsula (Ipoh Branch) and the Malaysian Youth Clubs Association (Teluk Intan Area).
Winners of the 2026 Perak State Special Youth Award received RM2,000 in cash, along with a trophy and certificate, in each of the seven contested categories: charisma, entrepreneurship, resilience, young volunteerism, sports, persons with disabilities, and uniformed associations. — Bernama

Title: Umno allows state leaders to negotiate cooperation with any party for next election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Umno has agreed to give its state leadership the mandate to hold discussions and negotiations with any political party interested in cooperating in the next election.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision was among the resolutions reached at the party’s Supreme Council meeting held last night.
“Any negotiations with any party to establish cooperation for the next election must be based on sincerity and trust, not by threatening,” he told a press conference after the meeting at Menara Dato’ Onn, World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here.
The meeting, which began at 8.45pm, was chaired by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and attended by deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Supreme Council members.
He said the meeting also agreed to extend an official invitation to PAS leaders to attend the 2026 Umno General Assembly, scheduled to take place from September 9 to 12.
Asyraf Wajdi said three programmes are also scheduled for Sept 8 — the 2026 Malay Education Convention, the Malaysian Islamic Scholars Convention and Laman Wanita Kreatif.
Meanwhile, he said Umno upholds the principle of the rule of law and stressed that no individual should be considered guilty until charged, tried and convicted by a court.
“Umno stresses that the party has consistently maintained that it will not defend any wrongdoing, misconduct or deviation by any party, including its members and leaders, who must face justice through due legal process,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Factory owner suffers first-degree burns trying to fight blaze that destroys 80pc of Butterworth premises
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A 58-year-old factory owner suffered first-degree burns to his hands and neck while trying to put out a fire that destroyed about 80 per cent of his fabric-processing premises in Jalan Bagan Ajam, Butterworth, yesterday evening.
Berita Harian
reported that the man was injured while attempting to tackle the blaze before being given initial treatment by Health Ministry personnel and taken to a nearby hospital for further treatment.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department Fire and Rescue Operations Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 6.09pm.
“The fire involved a semi-permanent factory that processes fabric for use in sofas.
“The blaze also damaged two motorcycles by about 50 per cent each, while a four-tonne lorry and a forklift were each about 90 per cent damaged.
“The fire was brought under control at 6.28pm, with firefighting efforts also assisted by nearby volunteer fire brigades and an excavator belonging to a private company,” he said in a statement today.
John said firefighters took nearly 10 hours to extinguish the blaze completely.
“The fire was fully extinguished at 4.35am today, after which overhaul work was carried out to ensure there were no other hazards,” he said.
The operation ended at 6.59am before the case was handed over to the Fire Investigation Division for further action.
A total of 26 personnel, including station chiefs, from the Butterworth, Penanti, Kepala Batas, Jalan Perak, Bandar Perda, Bertam and Perai fire and rescue stations were involved in the operation.

Title: UiTM must remain accessible to underprivileged Bumiputera students, says Sultan Sharafuddin
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 29 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah wants Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) to remain a gateway to social mobility for Malay and Bumiputera youths from low-income families and rural areas.
His Royal Highness said that as UiTM grew and progressed, the target group for whom the institution was originally established should not be left behind or distanced from higher education opportunities.
“The children of farmers, fishermen, drivers, factory workers, or poor rural families must continue to be assured that if they have the ability and determination to pursue knowledge, UiTM will provide the path to transform their future.
“That is the core spirit of UiTM’s struggle that must never be lost,” His Royal Highness said at the UiTM 2026 Royal Address at Dewan Konsert Seri Budiman here today.
Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, was also in attendance.
The event, organised by the Chair of the Malay Rulers Institution under the Adiwangsa Empowerment Office, was also attended by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the establishment of UiTM had paved a path that was previously difficult for many to access, adding that these efforts bore fruit after the institution, which formed the foundation of today’s UiTM, started in 1965 with only about 219 students and 11 lecturers.
His Royal Highness noted that within a decade, student enrolment grew to nearly 7,000 while teaching staff increased to about 1,000, with the university offering around 60 academic programmes and expanding branch campuses to several states.
“Today, UiTM has grown into one of the largest higher learning institutions in the country, producing more than 40,000 graduates annually, while its total alumni network has surpassed one million people.
“With such a vast network, I am confident the contributions of alumni can be leveraged to create a more significant impact. Therefore, I propose that a system be developed to enable each alumnus to contribute at least RM10 a month or RM100 a year to UiTM as a token of appreciation for the institution’s service during their studies.
“I believe a RM10 monthly contribution is not burdensome and can be afforded by every alumnus. Consider it a sacrifice to ensure the continuity and progress of UiTM,” said His Royal Highness.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the fund, with the potential to raise up to RM100 million annually, could be used for UiTM’s development and to assist new and existing students facing financial hardship.
“This is where the ‘UiTM Dihatiku’ slogan, often chanted by students, academic staff, and alumni, can be meaningfully demonstrated. Beyond the statistics are Malay and Bumiputera children from underprivileged backgrounds who have successfully transformed their lives through education at UiTM.
“Today, UiTM graduates are everywhere, in almost every industry and sector. They are accountants, engineers, doctors, lawyers, architects, academics, entrepreneurs, civil servants, corporate figures, artists, media practitioners, and leaders in various fields.
“Some of them lead major organisations, build businesses, create jobs, and contribute directly to national development.
“This is the true measure of UiTM’s success, not merely the number of students, graduates, or alumni, but the extent to which the institution has transformed lives and contributed to the nation’s progress,” His Royal Highness added. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak wakes to worsening haze as API breaches 200 in three locations
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 29 — Lubok Antu, Sri Aman and Lundu recorded very unhealthy air quality as of 8am on Saturday, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings of 225, 222 and 203 respectively.
According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s (NREB) Daily Haze Watch, these were the only three of the 18 monitoring locations statewide to record readings above 200.
Nine locations recorded unhealthy air quality, led by Serian at 193 and Sarikei at 188.
They were followed by Kuching at 169, Samarahan (168), Mukah (164), Tebedu (162), Sibu (160), Kapit (153) and Bintulu (151).
The remaining six locations recorded moderate air quality — Samalaju at 93, ILP Miri (70), Miri (68), Lawas (67), Bario (64) and Limbang (55).
An API reading of between 51 and 100 is classified as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, and 201 to 300 as very unhealthy. — The Borneo Post

Title: Govt to continue upholding UiTM’s role in Bumiputera development, says Zambry
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 29 — The government will continue to uphold Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) as a key institution in the educational, professional and socioeconomic development of the Bumiputera community.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the mandate and identity that formed the basis for UiTM’s establishment and development would continue to be preserved by the government.
“It is with the awareness of this great responsibility that I wish to affirm that the government will continue to defend UiTM as a key institution in the educational, professional and socioeconomic development of the Bumiputera community.
“The mandate and identity that formed the basis for UiTM’s establishment and development will continue to be preserved, but defending UiTM does not mean merely preserving what already exists. Instead, we must continue to strengthen, empower and advance it,” he said in his address at Majlis Titah Diraja UiTM 2026 held at Dewan Konsert Seri Budiman here yesterday.
Also in attendance at the ceremony, themed ‘Kecemerlangan Institusi Pendidikan Teras Pembangunan Negara’, were the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, and the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin.
Zambry said among the strategic measures implemented was the establishment of the UiTM Rationalisation Coordination Committee (URCC) to review academic, research, innovation, governance and talent development aspects.
He said the committee also covers industry linkages, internationalisation, and readiness to face future technological and economic changes, under the leadership of its chairman, Tan Sri Idris Jusoh.
“We want UiTM to continue developing as a ‘Premier University Driving Bumiputera Professionals’, with a strong mandate, high standards of excellence and broad contributions to the country and the world.
“In conjunction with UiTM’s 1956-2026 seven-decade evolution, themed ‘Legasi Ilmu, Aspirasi Unggul’, the achievements of these seven decades should not merely be celebrated but must be regarded as a responsibility to chart the next seven decades,” he said.
At the same time, Zambry stressed that the key question now was not merely how far UiTM had come, but rather the direction that the esteemed institution would take next. — Bernama

Title: Police detain seven Yemeni men after viral video of dangerous car stunt at Jalan Sungai Besi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police have detained seven Yemeni nationals to assist in investigations into an incident involving two cars being driven dangerously along Jalan Sungai Besi here early yesterday.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the men, aged between 23 and 26, were arrested in the capital and have since been released on police bail.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the incident occurred at about 12.30 am on Aug 28 while the two vehicles were travelling along Jalan Sungai Besi towards Jalan Bukit Bintang.
“Passengers in both vehicles were seen leaning their bodies out and dangerously sitting on the window frames while the vehicles were in motion.
“Five of those detained are students at a public university in Kedah, while the other two are university graduates,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Zamzuri said police questioning revealed that the dangerous stunt was carried out merely for fun in celebration of a friend’s wedding.
The case is being investigated under Section 336 of the Penal Code for negligent or rash acts endangering human life or the personal safety of others.
Upon conviction, the offence carries a penalty of up to three months’ imprisonment, a fine of up to RM500, or both.
Members of the public or witnesses with information about the incident are urged to come forward to assist in the investigation by contacting the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.
Earlier, a video of the incident went viral on social media, showing passengers in two cars leaning their bodies out and sitting on the window frames while the vehicles were being driven along Jalan Sungai Besi. — Bernama

Title: Nine years in remand, murder trial still at prosecution stage: Orang Asli man finally released
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — An Orang Asli man has been freed after spending nine years in remand while his murder trial was still at the prosecution stage, in a case his lawyer said had dragged on for far too long.
Sinar Harian
reported that Jambi Anak Chang Taa Nam, 47, was released by the High Court in Johor Bahru yesterday, ending almost a decade behind bars.
His lawyer, Kamal Hisham Jaafar, said Jambi had originally been charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code and had remained in custody as proceedings continued.
“Jambi was originally charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
“Although nine years have passed, the trial was still at the prosecution stage,” Kamal was quoted as saying.
He said the prolonged detention had also taken a toll on Jambi’s family life, leaving him with increasingly limited contact with his relatives.
Kamal, who handled the case
pro bono
, said he reviewed the evidence after taking over the case and subsequently submitted representations to the prosecution.
“The trial had gone on for far too long. When I came into the case, the prosecution was still presenting its case.
“So I showed the prosecution that the case against him was very weak,” he said.
According to Kamal, the charge against Jambi was subsequently amended from murder under Section 302 to an offence under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code, which covers culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Jambi was visibly emotional as Judge Atan Mustaffa Yussof Ahmad delivered the court’s decision before his release.
Kamal said his involvement in the case began only five months ago, after receiving a letter from Jambi in prison.
In it, Jambi reminded him that they had met 17 years earlier.
At the time, Jambi had accompanied his father, the
batin
, or village head, of an Orang Asli settlement in Johor to a Kembara Mahkota Johor programme, for which Kamal had served as programme secretary.
“After receiving the letter, I went to meet Jambi and decided to take on his case.
“Fortunately, things worked out in his favour. He hugged me and cried after finally regaining his freedom following years behind bars,” Kamal said.
In a Facebook post, Kamal said Jambi had previously been represented by several lawyers, all of whom later withdrew.
He also described Jambi as Malaysia’s “longest remand detainee”, although the claim could not be independently verified.

Title: Judiciary vital in upholding justice and people’s well‑being, says Tengku Maimun
Article:
BANGI, Aug 29 — The Judiciary is a vital institution and a key pillar in upholding justice, safeguarding the well-being of the people, and preserving the nation’s integrity, said former Chief Justice Tun Dr Tengku Maimun Tuan Mat.
She said the institution plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency and fairness under the Federal Constitution, while safeguarding the rule of law.
“Judges ensure that the rule of law is upheld, protect the fundamental rights of the people against any abuse of power, and reject all forms of misconduct through the system of checks and balances,” she said in her lecture titled ‘‘Integriti Pemangkin Jiwa Merdeka’ at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) here yesterday.
Tengku Maimun, a Professor of Practice at the UKM Faculty of Law (FUU), also holds the Tuanku Muhriz Royal Chair in Integrity and Good Governance.
The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, and the Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, graced the lecture.
Also present were UKM Pro-Chancellors Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tan Sri Datuk Rafiah Salim; Chairman of the UKM Board of Directors, Datuk Johan Idris; and UKM Vice-Chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Sufian Jusoh.
Tengku Maimun said the Judiciary’s critical role as the bulwark, protector, and guardian of the Constitution becomes increasingly evident when it ensures that no institution of the state, be it the executive or the legislative, exceeds the powers conferred upon it by the Constitution.
She noted that Malaysia upholds the principle of constitutional supremacy, rather than the doctrine of parliamentary sovereignty practised in the United Kingdom.
“Article 4(1) of the Federal Constitution also stipulates that any law enacted after Merdeka Day which is inconsistent with the Constitution shall, to the extent of the inconsistency, be void.
“This is where the critical role and heavy responsibility of the Judiciary lie, as the bulwark, protector, and guardian of the Constitution,” she said.
Tengku Maimun said the Judiciary’s role in safeguarding the rights and well-being of the people is reflected in various court rulings involving the right to a livelihood, environmental protection, freedom of speech, the customary land rights of the Orang Asli, and citizenship.
Meanwhile, she said integrity goes beyond merely refraining from corruption or complying with rules; rather, it is a commitment to doing what is right even when it is difficult, personally disadvantageous, or unpopular.
She said an organisational culture focused solely on superficial compliance could produce individuals who seek legal loopholes to evade punishment, whereas moral integrity demands that one asks what the right and proper course of action is.
According to her, integrity also hinges on an internal compass that compels a person to do what is right when no one is watching, as well as the ability to withstand external pressure, demands, and temptations.
She said fostering a culture of integrity requires consistency between words and actions, transparent monitoring systems, merit-based appointments, equitable enforcement of the law, and the firm imposition of penalties without fear or favour.
“Integrity, at its highest level, is the profound realisation that no personal secret, confidential document, off-the-record transaction, or hidden intention is shielded from His (God’s) scrutiny,” she said.
Tengku Maimun further said that the concept of Jiwa Merdeka (a liberated spirit) refers not merely to freedom from physical colonisation, but to a continuous and active process of liberation.
“Jiwa Merdeka is a continuous and active process of liberation. It demands the freedom of the mind to think rationally, freedom from the shackles of corruption, malfeasance, and moral decay, freedom from the tyranny of abuse of power, and freedom from ethical compromises that sacrifice personal dignity solely to preserve rank and position,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Prime Minister’s National Day 2026 address set for 2pm at PICC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — The 2026 National Day Prime Minister’s Address Ceremony at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here has been scheduled for 2 pm, according to the Ministry of National Unity (KPN).
In a statement yesterday, KPN said the adjustment was made after taking into account current developments, particularly to ensure the safety, health and comfort of guests and the public, in addition to ensuring the smooth implementation of the ceremony.
“The 2026 National Day Prime Minister’s 2026 Address Ceremony is an important platform to reflect on the aspirations and hopes of the Madani government leadership in fuelling the spirit of independence, strengthening patriotism, and nurturing a sense of love and responsibility towards the country.
“All Malaysians are invited to attend to celebrate the spirit of National Day and foster the values of mutual understanding, respect and acceptance of diversity towards building a nation that continues to progress, remain harmonious and prosper,” the statement said.
The National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 Celebration Working Committee under the Ministry of Communications had earlier announced that the Prime Minister’s address ceremony had been moved from Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur to PICC due to the current haze conditions.
It was previously reported that Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said hazy weather conditions were expected in Sabah from tomorrow, while high haze concentrations could occur in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya until August 31. — Bernama

Title: Why remand Kulai pair but not Perak MCA staff? Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng asks police after flag gaffe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng today accused the police of applying double standards in their handling of Jalur Gemilang cases, contrasting the four-day remand of two people in Kulai with the questioning, without detention, of those involved in an incident at the Perak MCA headquarters.
The DAP lawmaker called on the Inspector-General of Police to explain the difference in treatment, saying the IGP should resign or be removed if he failed to provide what Lim considered a reasonable explanation.
“The mistakes were almost identical, yet the police response was vastly different. Does police action depend on who is involved?” Lim said in a statement today.
His remarks came a day after Perak MCA apologised over the upside-down display of the Jalur Gemilang and Perak flag at its state headquarters in Ipoh.
Perak MCA state liaison committee chairman Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon said the mistake was unintentional and was corrected immediately after it was noticed.
He also said police officers visited the headquarters to investigate and record statements from the staff member involved and an administrative officer. The staff member later resigned.
Lim contrasted that case with the police response in Kulai, where he said two members of the public were detained and remanded for four days and also subjected to urine tests.
“In the Perak MCA case, those involved merely had their statements recorded without being detained,” he said.
Lim also cited an incident involving the Kuala Terengganu City Council, which displayed a Jalur Gemilang without the crescent and star. He said the explanation that it was a “technical error” was accepted and no arrests were reported.
“The Inspector-General of Police must immediately explain this double standard. If he fails to provide a reasonable answer or continues to remain silent, as in the Kulai case, he must resign or be dismissed immediately,” Lim said.
He said he did not believe anyone should be arrested over an incorrect display of the national flag if the mistake was genuinely unintentional, immediately corrected and followed by an apology.
“My position is clear. If a mistake involving the display of the Jalur Gemilang was genuinely unintentional, immediately corrected and followed by an apology, no one should be arrested,” he said.
“The police cannot act harshly against ordinary people while going easy on ‘VIPs’ and government agencies. That is not justice. That is favouritism.”

Title: Foreign Ministry says 36 Malaysians in Tibet reported safe, with checks widening to Chinese border areas
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Thirty-six Malaysians in Tibet, China have reported to be safe following flash floods and landslides in the China-Nepal border area.
Foreign Ministry deputy secretary-general (Bilateral Relations) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin said that the identities and status of the 36 Malaysians were still being verified with Chinese authorities, and they are cross-checking for any overlap with the list of Malaysians who remained uncontactable in Nepal.
“We are also conducting cross-checks because we have only just received this information... We will provide an update if there are any names that overlap, including the actual number of our citizens who are still missing or have been found safe, whether in Nepal or Tibet,” he told Bernama here yesterday.
Following the information, the ministry’s coordination efforts had now been expanded to cover areas on the Chinese side of the border, he added.
He shared that the Malaysian Embassy in Beijing and the Malaysian High Commission in New Delhi were also involved in the process as there was information that some Malaysians might have travelled along routes involving China and India.
The Foreign Ministry’s Operations Room in Putrajaya would continue to operate round the clock to coordinate information, assist Malaysians in the affected areas and provide the latest updates to family members, Syed Mohamad Hasrin said, adding that they would continue seeking confirmation from Chinese authorities regarding the whereabouts and safety of Malaysians in Tibet before drawing any further conclusions.
On the possibility of bringing affected Malaysians home, he said the matter needed to be coordinated with the Nepali authorities and tour operators, including verifying the status of their travel documents before any further action could be taken.
The priority at present was to locate Malaysians and ensure their safety in the affected areas, while taking into account weather conditions and limited access, he said.
In a related development, he said Malaysia, through the National Security Council (MKN) and the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), was coordinating and assessing the form of assistance that could be provided to Nepal.
Any assistance would take into account the needs identified by the Nepal government and would be subject to the consideration of MKN, as well as the acceptance and priorities of the Nepal government through official channels.
He said while Malaysia has expressed its readiness to assist Nepal, the Nepal government had so far indicated that it had sufficient resources to conduct search and rescue operations and required assistance could include financial resources and other forms of aid.
Nonetheless, Syed Mohamad Hasrin said the ministry is also assessing the readiness of Malaysian agencies, including the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team, while the Defence Ministry and the Malaysian Armed Forces were also ready to provide assistance.
Finally, in accordance with a decree by Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, the ministry would continue to provide affected Malaysians’ family members with the latest verified information.Syed Mohamad Hasrin said.
“At the same time, the media and public are urged not to speculate or disseminate unverified information, but instead refer to official statements from the Foreign Ministry for the latest updates,” he said.
Yesterday, Sultan Ibrahim urged Wisma Putra to take all necessary measures regarding Malaysians affected by the major floods in Rasuwa, Nepal. — Bernama

Title: PAS shuts door on Bersatu reconciliation, excludes Perikatan ally from muktamar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — PAS has declared that the door to reconciliation with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia within Perikatan Nasional (PN) has closed.
The rupture follows PAS’ accusation that its coalition partner contested against PN and signalled a willingness to work with Pakatan Harapan (PH).
PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the breakdown was also why Bersatu had not been invited to the Islamist party’s 72nd muktamar in Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan, from September 2 to 5.
“Yes, basically they [Bersatu] went against us in the Negeri Sembilan by-election, and there have been statements about wanting to work together with PH,” he was quoted as saying by
Utusan Malaysia
after delivering a
duha
lecture at Masjid Rusila in Marang yesterday.
Hadi was referring to Bersatu’s decision to contest against PN in the recent Negeri Sembilan by-election, as well as comments by party leaders that they were open to cooperation with PH ahead of the Melaka state election.
The dispute has deepened a rift between the two opposition parties, which remain formally within PN.
On June 8, a special meeting of the PAS central working committee decided to end political cooperation with Bersatu after reviewing the state and future direction of relations between the parties.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, PAS said the decision was reached after considering current reports, studies and assessments.
Hadi said PAS had instead invited Umno, as well as other parties in the PN coalition, to attend the
muktamar
.
The invitation comes as Umno has also extended an invitation to PAS’ top leadership to attend its general assembly in Kuala Lumpur from September 9 to 12.
The gathering will also focus on what PAS describes as ummah unity, with the party seeking broader cooperation with other political parties.
“We want to promote unity among Malay Muslims and non-Muslims who are not extremists,” Hadi said.
He added that PAS would use the gathering to strengthen its election machinery, saying a general election could be held in the near future as the current parliamentary term approaches its end.
“Another focus is to strengthen PAS’ election machinery as the general election is expected to be held in the near future, given that the current term is nearing its end.
“There must also be unity within the party. Our unity is strong; there is no internal crisis,” he said.
Bersatu Melaka information chief Hishamuddin Abdul Karim was meanwhile reported as saying the party remained open to discussions with other parties that shared common ground, including PH, ahead of the Melaka election.
He said, however, that any electoral cooperation should exclude parties that had betrayed the trust and spirit of cooperation previously established within PN.

Title: MetMalaysia issues special National Day forecast with thunderstorms, rain and haze expected through the weekend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a special weather forecast in conjunction with the 2026 National Day celebration, with several states set to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and haze on August 31.
According to a graphic posted on MetMalaysia’s Facebook page last night, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Johor are expected to experience thunderstorms in the morning, while Perak, Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan are forecast to have thunderstorms in the afternoon.
Rain is expected at night in Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan, while Perlis, Kedah and Penang are forecast to remain clear throughout the day.
Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan are expected to experience haze throughout the day.
In Sabah, thunderstorms and rain are expected to hit the interior and Sandakan throughout the day, while Tawau is expected to experience thunderstorms in the morning and rain at night.
The west coast of Sabah, meanwhile, is expected to experience haze throughout the day.
In Sarawak, most areas, including Kuching, Serian, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu, Mukah, Kapit, Bintulu and Miri, are expected to experience haze throughout the day.
Rain is expected to hit Kapit and Miri at night, while thunderstorms are forecast to hit Limbang in the afternoon, followed by rain at night.
In a separate post, MetMalaysia said most areas in the Klang Valley and along the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia are expected to be hazy on Sunday, the eve of the 2026 National Day celebration.
According to the special weather forecast graphic updated last night, hazy conditions are expected in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Labuan and Sarawak, as well as Kudat and the west coast of Sabah.
MetMalaysia also forecasts rain in Perak, Pahang, Terengganu, Kelantan and several areas in Sabah, including the interior, Sandakan and Tawau, on that night, while clear conditions are expected in Perlis, Kedah and Penang.
MetMalaysia advised those attending the National Day celebration on Sunday or the National Day parade on August 31 to check the weather forecast for their respective locations and take precautions in the event of changes in weather conditions. — Bernama

Title: Umno invites PAS top leadership to 2026 general assembly, returning muktamar gesture
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Umno will invite PAS’ top leadership to its general assembly next month, reciprocating an invitation extended to Umno leaders to attend the Islamist party’s annual
muktamar
in Kelantan.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the move was a gesture of respect towards PAS,
Sinar Harian
reported today.
“Umno has also agreed to extend an official invitation to PAS’ top leadership as a gesture of respect and to reciprocate the invitation extended to Umno’s leadership to attend the PAS annual
muktamar
,” he was quoted as saying at a press conference after an Umno Supreme Council meeting at Menara Dato’ Onn here yesterday.
The exchange of invitations comes ahead of a busy September for both parties, with PAS due to hold its 72nd annual
muktamar
from September 2 to 5, followed by the Umno general assembly from September 9 to 12.
PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan was previously reported to have invited several senior Umno leaders, including party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, to attend the
muktamar
.
Umno Youth chief Datuk Muhamad Akmal Saleh has also confirmed that he will attend the PAS Youth
muktamar
in Kota Bharu on September 3.
Separately, Asyraf Wajdi said Negeri Sembilan Umno liaison body deputy chairman and Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was appointed to the party’s supreme council with immediate effect.
Ismail took his oath of office before the Umno president and supreme council members before the meeting began.

Title: Muslims must lead by example through morality and integrity, says Anwar
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Aug 29 — Muslims must set the best example for society through good character, integrity, diligence and by rejecting corruption and wrongdoing, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the respect accorded to Muslims should stem from the positive values they demonstrate in daily life, including working diligently, keeping promises and not abusing positions of trust.
“If people see us working hard, displaying good character, not cheating and not stealing money, they will respect us. We must set a good example,” he said at a Maulid Akbar ceremony in conjunction with National Day at Masjid Tengah here yesterday.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan was also present.
Anwar said Islam carries a message of compassion and goodness for all, and Muslims must therefore safeguard relationships and the welfare of the entire community, regardless of race or religion.
The Prime Minister said Muslims must also demonstrate balance in life by prioritising knowledge, faith, morality, spiritual and physical development, as well as material progress.
He said the development of Malaysia Madani could not depend solely on policies, economic growth or technological advancement without a strong foundation of faith, morality and character.
“While reaching for the sky, we must remain rooted in the earth. Being rooted in the earth means having faith, morality and character, so that our values and moral principles are preserved,” he said.
Anwar also stressed the importance of seeking knowledge from Islamic scholars and strengthening ties between religious scholars and leaders through constructive advice and views.
Malaysia Madani must continue to drive economic growth and master modern technology, while ensuring that values and morality remain the pillars of national development, he added. — Bernama

Title: ‘Merdeka’ from fear and the courage to move forward together — Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz
Article:
AUGUST 29 — Every Merdeka and Malaysia Day, many in my and the older generation look back with pride at the founders of our nation. But August 31 and September 16 must be more than annual remembrances of 1957 and 1963. They should be moments when we ask ourselves a harder question: what kind of Malaysia do we want to build?
Nearly seven decades after Merdeka, and six decades after Malaysia Day, our nation — with her 34-million population — has become an industrialised, trading nation, a major part of global semiconductor supply chains, with millions of professionals. DOSM estimates that Malaysia had almost six million university graduates in 2024. Graduate unemployment had fallen to around 3.2 per cent.
Our forefathers built institutions, opened universities, created industries and expanded opportunities that previous generations could scarcely have imagined. Today, Malaysians of every community are doctors, engineers, scientists, lawyers, entrepreneurs, academics, executives, artists, programmers and innovators.
We should draw confidence from that progress. But why have our politics remained trapped in the anxieties of the past? The answer: fear — a powerful, and convenient agent. When people are worried about their economic future, it is easy to tell them that it is someone else’s fault and identity politics will safeguard their interests. It is easier to manufacture insecurity than to boost productivity. It is easier to identify an enemy than to create better jobs. It is easier to tell Malaysians what they should fear than to show them what they can become.
We must not allow irresponsible politicians to stoke our deepest insecurities. True political leadership should make people confident about the future, not trap them in fear. Younger Malaysians, especially, must resist this temptation.
Tengku Zafrul says that Malaysia must move beyond fear-based identity politics and focus instead on unity, social mobility, education, productivity and shared national progress. — Bernama pic
This does not require anyone becoming less Malay/Bumiputera, Chinese, Indian, Iban, Bidayuh, Kadazan-Dusun, Murut or anything else. Rather, we ought to be secure enough to realise that someone else’s identity does not threaten our own.
For Malays and Bumiputeras, this also means recognising how much we have progressed. Their participation in universities, professional sectors, entrepreneurship, government, business and technology have expanded enormously over the decades.
Admittedly, there remain inequalities that must be addressed. But cultivating a permanent sense of race-based fear or grievance will not resolve this. As the majority community, the Malays and Bumiputras should, by now, know what they are capable of. We can and will engage the world without fearing it.
And that same confidence should assure every Chinese, Indian, Sabahan and Sarawakian that this is also their country. This is the Malaysia we should aspire towards. Because the problems facing the next generation are colour-blind. Artificial intelligence will transform jobs. Climate change affects every household. The energy transition will reshape industries. Global supply chains are being reorganised. Major powers are competing for technology, investment and talent.
While we have achieved a labour market of more than 16 million people, the real challenge is to create sufficiently productive, skilled and well-paid jobs for the next generation. The median wage of Malaysian formal-sector employees is just over RM3,000 a month — not a huge contributor to our fiscal capacity. Income disparities have widened.
Those are challenges worthy of our political energy. What we should be obsessed with is upward social mobility. Getting people degrees is not enough. A university education is pointless if young graduates cannot break out of the low-income cycle, or cannot get jobs that match their skills.
Education remains one of Malaysia’s great engines of social mobility. But it needs a serious revamp in the face of a rapidly changing labour market. Tomorrow’s jobs require a new toolkit: digital literacy; problem-solving, technical and critical thinking skills; adaptability; effective communications, creativity and the ability to work alongside increasingly sophisticated technology.
Schools, universities, technical and vocational institutions, and employers must respond accordingly. Our measure of success must be whether each generation of Malaysians, through education and employment, can save, own a home and nurture their families. So, upward social mobility and expanding the middle class
should be the Government’s key priorities.
A confident Malaysia begins when the rakyat sees that hard work pays, that education can open doors and is open to everyone, and that a person’s origins aren’t their destiny. This is what will inspire hope in a society that tomorrow can be better than today.
That is why the questions we should be debating are: How do we raise wages? How do we distribute wealth more equitably? How do we reform our schools and universities’ syllabus for the unstoppable digital economy? How do we raise the productivity of Malaysian SMEs? How do we build internationally competitive companies? How do we ensure that all Malaysian children can fulfil their potential?
The answers to these questions will not come from the Malays or Bumiputeras alone. Or from any single race. They require the wisdom, energy and goodwill of all Malaysians. Our population’s diversity — something few countries have — is an advantage to be harnessed.
We are at home in South-east Asia, with a proven ability to build cultural and commercial bridges with most of the world at a time when the world is becoming more fragmented (think Asean Chairmanship in 2025!). But all this will go to waste if we keep distrusting each other due to fear-based politics.
Our greatest natural resource is not oil, gas or land. It is Malaysians. And yet we often waste our talent just because someone has the ‘wrong’ surname, comes from the ‘wrong’ state, worships differently or speaks another language.
Merdeka itself required extraordinary courage, as did forming Malaysia with Sabah and Sarawak in 1963. Our founders believed that different communities could build a country, together. They did not agree on everything. But they shared the conviction that they could only secure an independent Malaysia by working together.
Our generation needs that same courage again — to unite and work together to reject divisive politics, today’s ‘colonial masters’. We may continue to disagree about policies and politics. That is democracy. But that should not distract us from the fact that Malaysia’s challenges are too great, and the world is moving far too quickly, for us to waste another generation fearing each other over identity politics.
Today, Malaysians need a different ‘Merdeka’, a different Malaysia Day and a different Malaysia. We need true freedom from the politically motivated fears and insecurities that hold us back. We need the confidence to believe that unity against divisive, identity politics is what will make us stronger together. And the courage to rebuild a Malaysia that all Malaysians, in every state, truly deserve.
*Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz is senior political adviser to the prime minister and chairman of MIDA.
**This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of
Malay Mail
.

Title: A nation was born here: Stadium Merdeka keeps Malaysia’s independence story alive
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Nearly seven decades after witnessing the proclamation of independence, Stadium Merdeka remains a living symbol of Malaysia's freedom, a place that still remembers the day a nation was born.
Standing amidst the modern skyline beside the towering Merdeka 118 (Menara Merdeka Maybank), the stadium continues to serve as a vital connection to the nation’s history.
Built within a year at a cost of approximately RM2.3 million, the stadium was the setting for one of the nation’s defining moments -- the proclamation of Malaya’s independence on August 31, 1957, by the first Prime Minister Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj.
Universiti Putra Malaysia’s social anthropology expert Prof Dr Sarjit Singh Gill said Tunku Abdul Rahman’s seven resounding cries of “Merdeka!”, the first playing of Negaraku as the national anthem and the hoisting of the Jalur Gemilang marked the end of British colonial rule.
“This event marked the end of the British colonial era and the beginning of a new chapter for the Federation of Malaya. Stadium Merdeka is not merely a sports venue, but a historical monument that embodies the nation’s identity, dignity and rich heritage,” the Chairman of the National Council of Professors’ National Unity Cluster told Bernama.
In 1963, the stadium witnessed another historical moment, hosting the proclamation of the formation of the Malaysian Federation, effectively ending British colonial rule in Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore. (Singapore later separated)
Though the site faced redevelopment threats in the late 1990s, public opposition and government intervention ensured its survival. Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) took over the heritage site in 2000 to preserve the historical treasure.
PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd Chief Executive Officer Datuk Dr Izwan Ibrahim emphasised that preserving the stadium’s authenticity is paramount.
“Our approach is centred on preserving the authenticity of the stadium and ensuring its stories remain accessible to Malaysians. Stadium Merdeka is more than a reminder of the past, it represents the aspirations and determination that shaped the country we know today,” he said.
Once a venue for National Day celebrations, the stadium has evolved into a national landmark, now open to the public, featuring a refurbished track for community use and hosting cultural events like the Bazram Merdeka bazaar, a Ramadan Bazaar that attracted over 250,000 visitors earlier this year.
Izwan also highlighted the goal of engaging younger generations, encouraging them to experience the site firsthand rather than only learning about it in school and history books.
“For younger Malaysians, 1957 is something they may have learnt about in school or heard about from their parents and grandparents. But it is different when you are actually here.
“That is why we want young people to come to Stadium Merdeka and experience the place for themselves. We want them to use the space, take part in activities here and in the process, create their own connection with it. We are already seeing this happen with our neighbouring schools,” he said.
He said conservation works were guided by original Public Works Department construction drawings, and later additions like upper seating tiers were removed to restore the original 20,000-seat capacity, while features such as the scoreboard, washrooms, mosaic tiles and cantilevered roof were meticulously restored.
The stadium received a Unesco Asia-Pacific Heritage Award in 2008 and was gazetted as a National Heritage site in 2009.
For long-serving staff member Alias Daud, who spent the final 10 years of his 35-year PNB career caring for the venue, the site holds deep personal meaning, giving him a deep sense of pride and responsibility in preserving the national landmark for future generations.
“Every time I walk into Stadium Merdeka, I feel a mix of pride, gratitude and nostalgia. I have seen people from all walks of life come through its gates, each with their own stories and memories.
“It makes me happy to see this historic place continue to be appreciated and kept alive. Stadium Merdeka is more than a workplace to me. It feels like home,” he said.
Alias said the atmosphere became especially meaningful during national month, with government agencies, schools and universities visiting to learn about the stadium’s history and record Merdeka-related content.
He said visitors were often impressed to learn that Stadium Merdeka was where independence was proclaimed, with many reading about its history, taking photos and appreciating its significance, especially among younger visitors.
As modern skyscrapers now rise around it, Stadium Merdeka continues to stand as a powerful reminder of the moment Malaysia’s journey as a free and sovereign nation began, preserving the spirit of Merdeka for generations to come. — Bernama

Title: Bird-cage rooms and rooftop dorms expose Malaysia’s migrant housing enforcement gaps
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — From the outside, the 800-square-foot apartment unit looks no different from any other. Yet, what would normally be considered adequate accommodation for a family of five is home to 15 migrant workers.
Some employers are known to rent vacant flats, apartments or houses for their foreign workers, cramming as many of them as possible into each unit simply to cut costs, while failing to provide even basic amenities, including mattresses and kitchen equipment.
There are also landlords and property owners who modify the interiors of their units by either constructing dozens of tiny rooms or installing partitions to create cubicles for their tenants, most of whom are foreign workers.
Some have also resorted to constructing makeshift rooms, where space permits, on the rooftops of shop lots to accommodate foreign workers, particularly those employed in restaurants and supermarkets, and as general workers.
Workers from Myanmar, Vietnam and Cambodia interviewed by Bernama said they did not mind living under such conditions.
“I have to wake up as early as 3am to prepare the raw ingredients in the kitchen before the restaurant opens at 6am,” said Chin (not his real name), a Cambodian national working as a restaurant assistant in Puchong, Selangor.
“At night, after business operations end at 8pm, I have to clean the restaurant… my work only finishes at around 10pm. So, living upstairs makes things easier for me.”
The “hostel” he stays in is located on one of the upper floors of the building that houses the restaurant where he works. It has two rooms, with four male workers sharing one and four female employees the other, along with a bathroom and toilet.
“Originally, there was only one room, but the shop owner installed a partition to turn it into two rooms... we sleep on mattresses on the floor,” he said.
Rooms resembling bird cage pose safety risks
The trend of modifying apartments, shop lots and houses by installing partitions to create tiny cubicles — often metaphorically described as a bird’s cage, bird’s nest or grave — is worrying due to the serious safety risks involved.
The Ministry of Housing and Local Government has previously issued stern warnings to house and premises owners engaging in such practices.
Despite the enforcement of amendments to the Employees’ Minimum Standards of Housing, Accommodations and Amenities Act 1990 (Act 446) since 2020, which requires employers to provide their workers with comfortable accommodation and basic amenities, Bernama was informed by various stakeholders that the practice of cramming as many migrant workers as possible into cramped, modified residential units remains widespread.
Commenting on this, senior lecturer in real estate at the Faculty of Built Environment, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Shah Alam, Muhammad Azwan Sulaiman, said arbitrary modifications to premises could compromise occupants’ safety.
“From a technical and building safety perspective, having overly crowded rooms within a residential unit or premises can pose a serious fire risk.
“The problem is compounded by inadequate ventilation and lighting, turning such homes into potential death traps because, in the event of a fire, thick smoke can be more dangerous than the flames themselves, especially when occupants struggle to identify escape routes in an already congested space,” he told Bernama.
Muhammad Azwan said from an engineering perspective, the additional load arising from excessive numbers of occupants, furniture and electrical equipment could have long-term implications for the structural integrity and utility systems of buildings.
“Furthermore, electricity and water usage exceeding the building’s original design capacity not only increases the risk of electrical wiring-related hazards but can also shorten the building’s lifespan and increase maintenance costs,” he said, adding that the main problem with the practice of subdividing rooms is not the use of partitions but when the return on investment begins to take precedence over habitability and human lives.
Need for clear guidelines
Muhammad Azwan also proposed that the authorities establish clearer guidelines on the types of internal modifications permitted in stratified properties, particularly when such alterations involve the building’s basic structure or common property.
“The aim is not to prevent homeowners from carrying out renovations, but rather to reduce the risk of outset modifications.
“Good design at the planning stage can reduce unauthorised alterations, safety risks and disputes between occupants and management bodies,” he said.
He added that although Malaysia has various legal and regulatory frameworks governing worker accommodation, buildings and strata properties, one of the challenges is that supervisory and enforcement responsibilities fall under the jurisdiction of various agencies.
“This can create gaps in monitoring, particularly when a residential unit gradually becomes a high-density workers’ accommodation facility without obtaining the necessary approvals.
“Therefore, stronger inter-agency coordination, more effective monitoring and consistent enforcement are more important than simply introducing another new law,” he said.
Local authorities must act
While the government’s People’s Housing Projects (PPR) and public housing schemes intended for low-income Malaysians were previously targeted by employers seeking to house their workers, their attention has now shifted to medium-cost apartments and the upper floors of shop lots.
On Aug 3, local media reported that since 2023, 502 premises nationwide had been identified as having been extensively modified to create rental rooms, dubbed “bird’s nests”, that posed a high safety risk, particularly in the event of fire.
Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad was reported as saying that this practice was prevalent in major urban areas in Selangor, Penang and Johor, as well as Kuala Lumpur, due to the high demand for affordable accommodation among workers, students and middle-income groups.
Several integrated operations known as “Op Sarang Burung” conducted in the capital in June and Johor in July also found employers converting part of shop lot rooftops into hostels for foreign workers without approval from the authorities.
The operations in Kuala Lumpur were carried out by the Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department in collaboration with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the police.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh told Bernama in an interview that enforcement operations against residential units and premises illegally converted into rental rooms or hostels for foreign workers should be conducted regularly to ensure compliance with the law.
She said all local authorities should take the responsibility seriously, while close monitoring of enforcement personnel is also necessary to prevent abuse of power in the course of their duties.
“(In Kuala Lumpur) We need coordination among DBKL and the relevant enforcement agencies to ensure employers provide legal and suitable accommodation for their workers, while residential units under public housing schemes such as PPR remain available to families who are genuinely eligible and in need,” she said.
Comply with uniform building by-laws
Meanwhile, Ampang Jaya Municipal Council (MPAJ) deputy president Hasrolnizam Shaari told Bernama that safety aspects are always given priority before the council approves applications and renovation plans submitted by owners of business premises and residential properties.
He said any renovation that alters the layout, use of space or actual occupancy capacity would be assessed based on the Uniform Building By-Laws and the requirements of all local authorities, including MPAJ.
“We have demolished additional structures deemed to be highly risky as they could endanger occupants and the surrounding community because they might obstruct emergency access for fire engines and ambulances, besides causing disputes among residents.
“For structures that do not pose an immediate risk, we will continue to monitor them and take further action if they pose a threat to safety,” he added.
He said stubborn residential property owners who continue to carry out renovation and construction works without the approval of the local authority can be fined up to RM25,000 under Section 70(11) of the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974 (Act 133), while the court can order the local authority to alter or demolish the building.
Section 70(13)(d) of Act 133 further stipulates that any party who fails to comply with a lawful written order or directive issued by the local authority, or any limit or condition imposed by the local authority on renovation works, may be fined up to RM50,000, imprisoned for up to three years, or both.
He said MPAJ also adopts an integrated enforcement approach with other agencies, including the Immigration Department, police, State Health Department and the National Anti-Drugs Agency.
“Sometimes, a house has only one front door, but there are many occupants, both male and female, inside, with the space inside partitioned. So, we use an integrated enforcement approach to monitor and manage such situations,” he said.
Hasrolnizam said a slightly different approach is taken for renovations involving commercial premises, such as shop lots, as these properties are used for business activities.
“If the owner of a commercial lot wants to build seven or eight rooms, the application can be considered from a physical standpoint, but every room must have adequate lighting, ventilation and safety features, particularly in the event of a fire.
“They must first demonstrate that the design is acceptable and can be approved, and then obtain the necessary licence.
“However, if a business premises is found to be operating as a hostel without approval, it constitutes an offence and action can be taken,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Wisma Putra: Two Malaysians found safe after Nepal floods, 55 remain unreachable
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — Two of the 57 Malaysians previously reported as untraceable following flash floods and landslides in Nepal have been located, while 55 others remain unreachable as of 2.22pm today.
Foreign Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Bilateral Affairs) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin said the two Malaysians had been successfully located, but their information and details were still undergoing cross-checking and further verification.
“Out of the 57, two have been reported safe so far,” he told Bernama here today.
He said the cross-checking process was important to confirm the identity, location and actual status of both individuals, and to avoid duplication of information in the list of Malaysians who remained unreachable.
Syed Mohamad Hasrin said the figure of 55 was still subject to further verification based on information received from Nepalese authorities and relevant agencies.
He said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had instructed the ministry to continue monitoring the operations closely and step up efforts to locate the remaining Malaysians.
Following the directive, he said an official from the Malaysian High Commission in Dhaka had been dispatched to Kathmandu to help bolster the operations of the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal.
“The official is assisting in coordinating information, monitoring developments and liaising with the relevant Nepalese authorities,” he said.
