According to Syed Mohamad Hasrin, the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu was also collaborating with Nepalese authorities, the Nepalese Foreign Ministry’s emergency response team, the Nepal Tourism Board, relevant agencies and tour operators to obtain and verify information regarding the untraceable Malaysians.
Nepalese authorities reported that 528 individuals had been rescued so far, comprising 490 Nepalese and 38 foreigners. Based on the latest information received, no Malaysians have been identified among those rescued.
The flash floods and landslides in the Rasua district occurred following the overflow of the Bote Koshi River on August 26, causing severe damage to infrastructure, including roads and bridges, as well as disrupting electricity supply and communication networks.
“This situation has made access to the affected areas difficult, thus hampering search and rescue efforts and the gathering of information on Malaysians in those areas,” he said.
Syed Mohamad Hasrin said the ministry was also monitoring safety warnings issued by Nepalese authorities regarding the risk of water overflows from the border areas.
He said the situation in the affected areas remained challenging and safety conditions could change rapidly, while search and rescue operations also faced constraints due to weather conditions and infrastructure damage.
“We are hoping for the best. But under these conditions, it is quite difficult. Their authorities are also dealing with their own affected citizens. The situation is severe, with cut-off roads, damaged bridges and so on,” he said.
The Foreign Ministry’s operations room in Putrajaya is now operating 24 hours a day to coordinate information, assist Malaysians in the affected areas and provide updates to family members.
According to Syed Mohamad Hasrin, every call and piece of information received must be cross-checked with the lists from Nepalese authorities and the ministry’s internal records to avoid duplication or confusion.
The number of unreachable Malaysians was obtained from various sources, including Nepalese authorities, Nepal Tourism Board, tour operators and family members.
Within the first two to three hours after the operations room was activated, the ministry received between 12 and 15 calls from family members and friends seeking information on Malaysians believed to be in Nepal.
The ministry urged family members with relevant information to contact the operations room, providing details such as full names, passport numbers, travel itineraries, last known locations and contactable phone numbers.
Malaysians with relevant information can contact the Putrajaya Operations Room at +603 8887 4570 or email dutyofficer@kln.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: ‘False and baseless’: Teo Nie Ching rejects social media claims linking her to Johor gang activity, lodges police report
Article:
KULAI, Aug 28 — Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching today denied allegations circulating on social media linking her to gang-related activities in the state and a road accident currently under police investigation.
The DAP national vice-chairman said the allegations were false and baseless, stressing that new social media accounts had been created specifically to make accusations against her.
“I have been in politics for 18 years and have served as a MP for 13 years. There may have been occasions when I met someone once or twice, or perhaps had photographs taken with someone in an ordinary social setting.
“However, to claim that I was involved in such activities is a false accusation because they merely showed photographs of me with someone, when it was simply a normal social activity.
“The police, including the Johor police chief, have already held a press conference and announced that 13 suspects had been arrested. I welcome a thorough investigation by the police,” she told reporters after the Safe Internet Campaign Community Carnival at Hutan Bandar Putra here today.
Teo, who is also Johor DAP chairman, said the defamatory claims demonstrated that anyone could become a victim of the spread of fake news in the digital era.
She therefore advised the public not to readily believe information received through social media without verifying it first.
“We need to think rationally and investigate first. I myself have lodged a complaint with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) as well as a police report.
“However, the main challenge is that the decision to shut down the account or delete the post rests with Meta, and not all fake news can be removed immediately,” she said.
Yesterday, Senai assemblyman Wong Bor Yang lodged a police report at the Kulai District Police Headquarters here over defamatory posts and false allegations linking Teo and DAP to a gang. — Bernama

Title: Stulang assemblyman Andrew Chen returns to lead Johor Opposition after bruising state election
Article:
KULAI, Aug 28 — Johor Pakatan Harapan (PH) has agreed to appoint Stulang state assemblyman Andrew Chen Kah Eng as Johor’s Leader of the Balancing Force (Ketua Pengimbang).
Johor DAP chairman Teo Nie Ching said the appointment had been agreed by all three PH component parties: DAP, PKR and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah).
“DAP proposed Andrew Chen Kah Eng as the Opposition Leader, or Leader of the Balancing Force, in Johor, and the proposal was accepted by our partners from PKR and Amanah,” she told reporters after the Safe Internet Campaign Community Carnival at Hutan Bandar Putra here today.
Andrew also held the position during the previous Johor state government’s 2022-2026 term, before the state assembly was dissolved on June 1.
In the 16th Johor state election held on July 11, Barisan Nasional formed the new state government after winning 48 seats, while PH secured eight. — Bernama

Title: Johari Abdul calls for diplomacy to prevent Cambodia-Thailand dispute from straining Asean
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Dialogue and diplomacy must continue to be prioritised in addressing the Cambodia-Thailand border issue to ensure regional peace and stability, said Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul.
He said the approach is important to ensure that bilateral issues do not undermine the spirit of togetherness and unity within Asean, which serves as a platform for member states to build trust, seek common ground and manage differences constructively.
Johari said the border issue was among the matters discussed during his meeting with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet on the sidelines of the Second Inter-Parliamentary Speakers’ Conference (ISC-2) in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.
“Developments along the Cambodia-Thailand border were also among the matters given attention. Malaysia understands Cambodia’s concerns over the current situation, including its impact on residents in the affected areas.
“In this regard, I stressed that dialogue and diplomacy must always be given space in addressing any differences among Asean member states,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Johari is in the Cambodian capital to attend the conference, jointly hosted by Cambodia’s National Assembly and Senate from August 26 to 28.
He said Malaysia would continue to support efforts to bring all parties back to the negotiating table, with priority given to ensuring that regional peace and stability are preserved.
During the meeting, both sides also exchanged views on strengthening Malaysia-Cambodia ties, covering parliamentary cooperation, the economy, human capital development and youth empowerment.
He said youth from both countries should be given more opportunities to build ties through exchange programmes and participation in the economic, social and inter-parliamentary spheres.
He said the potential to expand cooperation in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) was also discussed, including via skills training, institutional exchanges and industry collaboration.
At the same time, Johari also expressed appreciation for the Cambodian government’s role in facilitating the operations and investments of Malaysian companies in the country, thereby providing a conducive environment for the Malaysian business community.
He added that Malaysia is committed to continuing close cooperation with Cambodia to strengthen the long-standing bilateral ties for the sake of peace, stability and shared prosperity of the Asean region. — Bernama
